# ---------------- G. INDEMNITY / LOL ----------------
dict(id="D-35", area="G. Indemnification and Limitation of Liability",
 title="Indemnification obligations carved OUT of the liability cap (uncapped), reversing the Term Sheet's express statement that indemnity is within the cap",
 ref="TS §10, §11 / EL §9.2",
 ts="\"For the avoidance of doubt, indemnification obligations under Section 10 are subject to and included within the aggregate liability cap.\" Only exclusions: confidentiality breaches; willful misconduct or fraud.",
 el="Cap does not apply to \"(A) a Party's indemnification obligations under Section 9.1,\" confidentiality breaches, or willful misconduct/fraud. The consequential-damages waiver also does not apply to these carve-outs.",
 sev="Dealbreaker", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=[
  "The indemnity is mutual in form but asymmetric in substance: Stellarion is the party contributing the core licensed IP, which Helix will distribute worldwide to a base of approximately 3,400 enterprise customers, so Stellarion's IP indemnity is the obligation most likely to be called. Removing it from the cap, and from the consequential-damages waiver, exposes Stellarion to unlimited liability, including customers' consequential damages passed through as \"third-party claims\", in exchange for a $12.5 million upfront fee. For a company with $67.3 million ARR, a single significant patent assertion against Helix's installed base could exceed Stellarion's total consideration under the deal and threaten solvency.",
  "The Term Sheet language was explicit (\"for the avoidance of doubt ... included within\"), so this is a direct reversal of a negotiated point, not a gap-fill.",
 ],
 position="Reject. Restore: indemnification obligations are subject to and included within the aggregate cap. If Helix insists on separate treatment, the most Stellarion should consider is a separate IP indemnity super-cap (e.g., the greater of fees paid in the prior 24 months or a fixed amount not exceeding the $25 million general cap), with customary exclusions and remedies (see D-37)."),

dict(id="D-36", area="G. Indemnification and Limitation of Liability",
 title="Aggregate liability cap reduced from $25,000,000 to $20,000,000",
 ref="TS §11 / EL §9.2",
 ts="$25,000,000 aggregate cap per party.",
 el="$20,000,000 aggregate cap per party.",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=[
  "With indemnity carved out (D-35), a lower cap principally limits what Stellarion can recover from Helix, for example for Helix's misuse of EdgeAI outside the field, breach of the non-compete, unauthorized sublicensing, or non-payment, while Stellarion's own largest exposure (indemnity) is uncapped. The combination is doubly adverse. Note also that, as drafted, Helix's unpaid fees and royalties could themselves count toward the cap.",
 ],
 position="Restore $25,000,000 and add an express carve-out so that Helix's payment obligations (upfront fee, royalties, minimum royalty) are not limited by or counted toward the cap."),

dict(id="D-37", area="G. Indemnification and Limitation of Liability",
 title="Indemnity scope broadened (\"infringes, misappropriates, or otherwise violates\"; \"arising out of or relating to\"; successors and assigns) without customary IP indemnity exclusions or remedies",
 ref="TS §10 / EL §9.1",
 ts="Indemnity for third-party claims \"arising from alleged infringement of intellectual property rights by the indemnifying party's Background IP\"; procedures to be detailed in the Definitive Agreement; subject to the cap.",
 el="Indemnity for Losses \"arising out of or relating to any claim that the Indemnifying Party's Background IP, as contributed to or utilized in the arrangement ... infringes, misappropriates, or otherwise violates\" third-party IP; Indemnified Parties include successors and assigns. No exclusions; no mitigation remedies.",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=[
  "Adding misappropriation and \"otherwise violates\" (trade secret, moral rights, etc.) broadens Stellarion's exposure beyond infringement. \"As ... utilized in the arrangement\" extends coverage to EdgeAI as integrated, modified and combined by Helix. The letter omits the standard licensor protections: no indemnity for claims caused by (a) Helix modifications (Helix has a modification right under EL §4.1), (b) combination with Helix Edge Runtime or other non-Stellarion technology where the claim would not arise but for the combination, (c) use outside the Licensed Field or in breach of the Agreement, (d) continued use after Stellarion provides a non-infringing update; and no right for Stellarion to procure a license, modify or replace, or terminate and refund as its sole obligation. Including \"successors and assigns\" matters given the free M&A assignment right (D-54).",
 ],
 position="Limit to infringement or misappropriation by EdgeAI as delivered by Stellarion and used in accordance with the Agreement; add the customary exclusions and remedies (procure/modify/replace/terminate); keep within the cap (D-35)."),

dict(id="D-38", area="G. Indemnification and Limitation of Liability",
 title="Indemnification procedures added (prompt notice with prejudice standard; control of defense; settlement consent)",
 ref="TS §10 (procedures to Definitive Agreement) / EL §9.1",
 ts="Standard procedures to be set out in the Definitive Agreement.",
 el="Prompt notice (failure excuses only to the extent of material prejudice); indemnitor controls defense with counsel reasonably acceptable to indemnitee; indemnitee \"shall cooperate fully\"; no settlement imposing obligations or lacking full release without consent.",
 sev="Minor", favors="Neutral", action="Accept",
 analysis=["Market-standard and mutual. Minor refinements: cooperation should be at the indemnitor's expense; indemnitor's control should not be conditioned on counsel being \"reasonably acceptable\" (or the standard should be stated objectively)."],
 position="Accept with minor refinements."),

dict(id="D-39", area="G. Indemnification and Limitation of Liability",
 title="Consequential damages waiver expressly includes lost profits and revenue, with no carve-out for license-scope, field-of-use, non-compete, sublicensing or payment breaches",
 ref="TS §11 / EL §9.2 (second paragraph)",
 ts="Mutual waiver of indirect, incidental, consequential, special or punitive damages. Exclusions from the cap: confidentiality; willful misconduct or fraud.",
 el="Waiver expanded to \"exemplary\" damages and expressly to \"loss of profits, loss of revenue, loss of data, loss of business opportunity, or loss of goodwill\"; excepted only for the cap carve-outs (indemnity, confidentiality, willful misconduct/fraud).",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=[
  "Stellarion's principal damages if Helix deploys EdgeAI in supply chain optimization, breaches the non-compete, or sublicenses without consent would be lost profits in its core market. The Engagement Letter's express inclusion of lost profits and lost business opportunity in the waiver would bar most of that recovery, leaving Stellarion with injunctive relief (which, under the exclusive arbitration clause, is itself uncertain; see D-53). The Term Sheet waiver had the same basic architecture, so part of this is a gap common to both documents; but the express listing of lost profits makes the Engagement Letter materially worse.",
 ],
 position="Carve out from both the cap and the consequential damages waiver: (i) Helix's use of EdgeAI or Joint IP outside the scope of the license (including the Excluded Field), (ii) breach of the non-compete and sublicensing restrictions, (iii) infringement or misappropriation of the other party's IP, and (iv) payment obligations. At a minimum, delete the express reference to lost profits/revenue for these categories."),

dict(id="D-40", area="H. Confidentiality",
 title="Confidentiality survival cut from 3 years to 2 years",

dict(id="D-41", area="H. Confidentiality",
 title="\"Confidential Information\" narrowed (designated or reasonably understood as confidential); exceptions loosened; permitted recipients expanded to consultants and contractors",
 ref="TS §14 / EL §3 (\"Confidential Information\"), §10.1",
 ts="All non-public technical, business, financial and other information disclosed in connection with the transactions, in any form. Prior-knowledge exception requires evidence by written records; public-domain exception requires no breach by the recipient. Disclosure permitted to employees, directors, advisors and professional representatives with need to know.",
 el="Information \"designated as confidential or that ... reasonably should be understood to be confidential\"; prior-knowledge exception without written-records requirement; public-domain exception \"through no fault\"; disclosure permitted also to \"officers, ... consultants, and contractors\" bound by written obligations; compelled-disclosure exception added; terms of the Agreement expressly confidential.",
 sev="Moderate", favors="Mixed (net Helix)", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=[
  "The marking/reasonable-understanding test is common but narrower than the Term Sheet's \"all non-public information\" formulation and shifts the burden to Stellarion in a dispute.  ],

# ---------------- I. TERMINATION ----------------
dict(id="D-43", area="I. Termination",
 title="Breach termination: 30-day notice running concurrently with 30-day cure (effective approximately 30 days) instead of 60-day notice and 30-day cure (90 days total); \"material breach ... of any material provision\"",
 ref="TS §12.1 / EL §11.1",
 ts="60 days' written notice; 30-day cure period; termination effective on expiry of cure period, \"i.e., ninety (90) days total from delivery of the initial notice of breach.\"",
 el="Termination on 30 days' prior written notice for \"a material breach ... of any material provision,\" if the breach remains uncured 30 days after receipt of notice.",
 sev="Moderate", favors="Mixed", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=[
  "The Engagement Letter compresses the termination timeline from about 90 days to about 30. Because the right is mutual, the effect cuts both ways: it lets Stellarion terminate faster for Helix's breach (e.g., non-payment, field-of-use violations), but it also exposes Stellarion to rapid termination by Helix (for example, over a Meridian performance dispute) shortly after Stellarion has deposited source code and committed development resources. The double materiality qualifier (\"material breach\" of a \"material provision\") raises the bar for terminating and is generally unhelpful to the licensor.",
  "Term Sheet drafting note: TS §12.1 is internally inconsistent: a 30-day cure period running \"following receipt of such notice\" would expire on day 30, not day 90. The parenthetical shows the intended reading (60-day notice period followed by 30-day cure); the Definitive Agreement should state the mechanics unambiguously.",
 ],
 position="Negotiate a split regime: (i) payment defaults: 15–30 day cure, then immediate termination; (ii) breaches of the field-of-use, sublicensing, confidentiality or non-compete provisions: termination on 30 days' notice if uncured (or immediately if not curable or willful); (iii) all other material breaches: the Term Sheet's 90-day framework. Delete \"of any material provision.\""),

Note that ipso facto termination rights may be unenforceable against a debtor under the U.S. Bankruptcy Code, and Helix as licensee would have rights under 11 U.S.C. §365(n) if Stellarion were the debtor; neither point is a reason to reject the clause."],

dict(id="D-45", area="I. Termination",

dict(id="D-9", area="B. License Grant, Field of Use and Term",
 title="Renewal: two 3-year renewal terms (maximum 11 years) instead of two 2-year terms (maximum 9 years); non-renewal notice shortened from 180 to 120 days",

 ts="Two successive 2-year renewals; maximum total term 9 years; non-renewal notice at least 180 days before expiry.",

 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=[

 ],

# ---------------- C. FINANCIAL ----------------
dict(id="D-10", area="C. Financial Terms",
 title="Upfront fee installments restructured from $7.5M / $5.0M to two equal $6.25M installments",
 ref="TS §4.1 / EL §5.1",
 ts="$12,500,000 total: $7,500,000 due upon execution of the Definitive Agreement; $5,000,000 due on the six-month anniversary.",
 el="$12,500,000 total: $6,250,000 within 10 business days following execution of the Definitive Agreement; $6,250,000 on the six-month anniversary.",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=[
  "The headline number is unchanged, which makes this easy to miss on a skim. But $1,250,000 is moved from the signing installment to the six-month installment, increasing Stellarion's credit exposure to Helix on the deferred tranche from $5.0 million to $6.25 million (a 25% increase) and deferring cash Stellarion was counting on at closing. Illustratively, at an 8% annual cost of capital the time-value cost of the shift alone is roughly $48,000, before considering credit risk and the additional 10-business-day delay on the first installment (D-11).",
  "Stellarion's protection on the deferred tranche is also weak: there is no acceleration on Helix termination, assignment or change of control, and no late-payment interest outside the audit context (D-19).",
 ],
 position="Restore $7,500,000 on execution and $5,000,000 at six months. Add that the second installment accelerates on any termination by Helix (other than for Stellarion's uncured breach), any termination by Stellarion for Helix's breach or insolvency, and any assignment by Helix under the M&A exception."),

dict(id="D-11", area="C. Financial Terms",
 title="First installment payable \"within ten (10) business days following\" execution instead of \"upon execution\"; wire instructions deadline",

 ts="First installment due upon execution of the Definitive Agreement. Payment by wire to an account designated by Stellarion in writing.",
 el="First installment due within 10 business days after execution. Stellarion must provide wire instructions at least 5 business days before the payment date.",
 sev="Moderate", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=[
  "Up to two additional weeks of delay on $6.25 million (or $7.5 million once restored), during which Helix would already hold the license. The wire-instruction requirement is sensible operationally but, as drafted, could be argued to be a condition to Helix's payment obligation (a late instruction letter could push the due date).",
 ],
 position="Payment due upon (concurrently with) execution of the Definitive Agreement. Stellarion will deliver wire instructions at signing; clarify that any delay in delivering instructions extends the due date only day-for-day and does not otherwise excuse payment."),

dict(id="D-12", area="C. Financial Terms",
 title="Royalty base changed from Net Revenue (received, less returns, allowances, trade discounts, sales taxes) to Gross Revenue (GAAP-recognized revenue of Helix and its Affiliates, before any deductions)",
 ref="TS §4.2 / EL §3 (\"Gross Revenue\"), §5.2",
 ts="4.5% of Net Revenue: \"gross revenue actually received by Helix ... less returns, allowances, trade discounts, and sales taxes actually incurred.\"",
 el="4.5% of Gross Revenue: \"all revenue recognized by Helix or its Affiliates\" from products and services that \"incorporate or utilize\" EdgeAI, under GAAP, \"prior to any deductions for returns, allowances, discounts, shipping, taxes, or other adjustments.\"",
 sev="Minor", favors="Stellarion", action="Accept",
 analysis=[
  "This deviation favors Stellarion: the rate is unchanged but the base is larger (no deductions), includes Affiliate revenue, covers products that merely \"utilize\" EdgeAI, and is measured on recognition rather than cash receipt. Illustratively, on $50 million of attributable gross revenue with 8% of deductions, the Engagement Letter royalty is $2.25 million versus $2.07 million under the Term Sheet (about $180,000 per year more).",
  "Caution: (i) Helix's counsel may have intended this as a trade for other concessions (e.g., the lower minimum royalty), or it may be a drafting error Helix will reverse once flagged; (ii) recognized-revenue timing for subscription offerings is ratable, which can defer royalties relative to billings; (iii) \"attributable to\" is undefined, so for bundled Helix Edge Runtime offerings Helix will argue for an allocation of only a fraction of the bundle price. The Definitive Agreement needs an allocation methodology (e.g., royalty on the full price of any SKU that includes EdgeAI functionality, or a fixed minimum per-unit royalty).",
  "Negotiating posture: because Stellarion's overall message is \"conform to the Term Sheet,\" insisting on keeping a Stellarion-favorable deviation slightly weakens that message. We recommend retaining Gross Revenue in the redline but treating it as a tradable item that can be conceded (reverting to Net Revenue) in exchange for restoration of the dealbreaker items.",
 ],
 position="Accept (retain) in the redline; add a bundled-revenue allocation rule and extend audit rights to Affiliates. Be prepared to revert to Term Sheet Net Revenue as a give."),

dict(id="D-15", area="C. Financial Terms",
 title="Minimum Annual Royalty reduced from $3,000,000 to $2,500,000",
 ref="TS §4.3 / EL §5.3",
 ts="Minimum annual royalty of $3,000,000 from Year 2 onward, including renewal periods.",
 el="Minimum Annual Royalty of $2,500,000 from the second year of the License Term onward.",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=[
  "A 16.7% reduction in Stellarion's guaranteed floor: $500,000 less per Royalty Year. Over the Initial Term (Royalty Years 2 through 5) the guaranteed floor drops from $12.0 million to $10.0 million (a $2.0 million reduction). Over a full nine-year Term Sheet term (Years 2 through 9) the reduction at the Term Sheet structure would be $4.0 million. (Under the Engagement Letter's own eleven-year maximum the floor is $25.0 million over ten Royalty Years, but that figure reflects two extra years of license, not a better deal.)",

 ],

dict(id="D-17", area="C. Financial Terms",

# ---------------- D. MERIDIAN ----------------
dict(id="D-20", area="D. Project Meridian Co-Development",
 title="New joint Steering Committee with authority to set milestones, approve work plans, allocate resources and resolve disputes; no deadlock mechanism",
 ref="TS §5.1 / EL §6.1",
 ts="Joint development plan (specifications, milestones, staffing, acceptance criteria) to be set out in the Definitive Agreement or a statement of work; potential integration into \"other authorized products as mutually agreed.\"",
 el="Equal-representation Steering Committee responsible for \"setting milestones, approving work plans, allocating resources, and resolving any disputes.\" Reference to other authorized products omitted.",
 sev="Moderate", favors="Neutral / ambiguous", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=[
  "A steering committee is customary, but as drafted (i) \"allocating resources\" could be read to let the committee commit Stellarion personnel and spending, which combined with the uncapped overrun mechanism (D-22) creates open-ended exposure; (ii) there is no voting rule or deadlock-breaking mechanism; and (iii) committee \"dispute resolution\" sits uneasily with the exclusive arbitration clause (EL §15.2).",
 ],
 position="Accept a Steering Committee with: unanimous decisions; no authority to amend the Agreement, increase the budget, or commit either party's resources beyond the approved plan; escalation to the CEOs within 15 business days, then arbitration; and no ability to waive the field-of-use, sublicensing or IP provisions."),

 ts="$8,200,000 budget: Helix 60% ($4,920,000); Stellarion 40% ($3,280,000).",

 analysis=["Shifts $410,000 of budgeted cost to Stellarion (a 12.5% increase in Stellarion's share), and the same 45% ratio applies to every overrun dollar (D-22). Arithmetic in the Engagement Letter is internally correct (55% and 45% of $8.2 million)."],
 position="Restore 60/40 ($4,920,000 / $3,280,000)."),

dict(id="D-22", area="D. Project Meridian Co-Development",
 title="Cost overruns automatically shared pro rata; Term Sheet requirement of mutual written approval for overruns above 10% deleted",
 ref="TS §5.2 / EL §6.2",
 ts="\"Any cost overruns exceeding ten percent (10%) of the estimated budget shall require mutual written approval of both parties before such overruns are incurred.\"",
 el="\"Costs incurred in excess of the Project Budget shall be allocated between the Parties in the same proportion ... (i.e., 55% to Helix and 45% to Stellarion), unless otherwise agreed by the Parties in writing.\"",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=[
  "This removes Stellarion's veto over budget growth and makes its exposure uncapped. Illustration: a 25% overrun ($2,050,000) would cost Stellarion $922,500 under the Engagement Letter with no approval right, versus a requirement for Stellarion's prior written approval under the Term Sheet (and 40% sharing, $820,000, only if approved). Combined with the Steering Committee's \"allocating resources\" authority (D-20) and the invoicing mechanics (D-23), Helix could drive spending that Stellarion must fund.",
 ],
 position="Restore the Term Sheet rule: no party is obliged to fund, and no party may incur as a shared cost, any overrun above 10% of the budget without both parties' prior written approval; overruns within the 10% band shared 60/40."),

dict(id="D-23", area="D. Project Meridian Co-Development",
 title="Personnel cost rule omitted; reciprocal quarterly invoicing for \"costs incurred\" (scope of shared costs undefined)",
 ref="TS §5.2 / EL §6.2",
 ts="Each party bears its own personnel costs (salaries, benefits, overhead); only shared costs (third-party tools, cloud infrastructure, testing services) are split; allocation quarterly per the plan.",
 el="Each party invoices the other quarterly \"for the other Party's share of costs incurred during the preceding quarter,\" payable within 30 days. No statement that personnel costs are borne by each party.",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=[
  "Without the Term Sheet's personnel-cost rule, either party can argue that its internal engineering, benefits and overhead are \"costs incurred\" on Project Meridian and invoice the other party for its percentage. Helix, as the far larger organization (approximately $1.2 billion revenue), is better positioned to load costs (including overhead allocations) into the pool. The Term Sheet carefully limited cross-charging to true third-party shared costs.",
 ],
 position="Restore: \"Each Party shall bear its own personnel costs (including salaries, benefits and overhead). Only Shared Costs (third-party tools, cloud infrastructure and testing services, in each case incurred in accordance with the approved plan and supported by third-party invoices) shall be allocated 60% to Helix and 40% to Stellarion.\" Add audit rights over the other party's shared-cost invoices."),

dict(id="D-24", area="D. Project Meridian Co-Development",
 title="JOINT IP SUBLICENSING: prior written consent requirement deleted; each party may \"license\" Joint IP without consent [GC PRIORITY 2]",
 ref="TS §5.3 / EL §6.3",
 ts="Each party may exploit Co-Developed IP without consent or accounting, \"subject to the restriction set forth below. However, neither party may sublicense jointly-owned Co-Developed IP to any third party without the prior written consent of the other party.\" Consent not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed.",
 el="\"Each Party shall have the right to exploit, use, license, and otherwise commercialize the Joint IP without the consent of, or any obligation to account to, the other Party.\" No sublicensing restriction.",
 sev="Dealbreaker", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=["(See Part IV.2 for full analysis.)"],

dict(id="D-25", area="D. Project Meridian Co-Development",
 title="\"Joint IP\" narrowed to IP jointly conceived by both parties' personnel; IP developed by one party in Project Meridian falls outside joint ownership",
 ref="TS §5.3 (\"Co-Developed IP\") / EL §3 (\"Joint IP\"), §6.3",
 ts="\"All intellectual property arising from Project Meridian, including all inventions, discoveries, improvements, works of authorship, software, algorithms, and related documentation\" is jointly owned.",
 el="Joint IP = IP \"conceived, created, developed, or reduced to practice jointly by employees or contractors of both Parties in the course of, and arising from, Project Meridian.\" No rule for IP created by one party alone.",
 sev="Material", favors="Ambiguous (likely Helix)", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=[
  "Under the Term Sheet, everything arising from Project Meridian is joint. Under the Engagement Letter, only jointly-conceived IP is joint; Meridian work product created by one party's team alone is not addressed and would, by default, belong to the creating party. Helix is likely to perform most of the integration engineering on Helix Edge Runtime, so this gap could leave Helix as sole owner of significant Meridian deliverables, free of any sublicensing restriction at all.",
  "The narrowed definition also matters for the Background IP boundary (D-27): improvements to EdgeAI made by Stellarion alone during Meridian would fall outside \"Joint IP\" (good for Stellarion), but may also fall outside Stellarion \"Background IP\" if any Helix \"resources\" were used.",
  "Related point present in both documents: neither the Term Sheet nor the Engagement Letter carves out improvements to, or derivatives of, a party's Background IP from co-developed IP. Under the Term Sheet's broad definition, improvements to EdgeAI arising from Meridian would be jointly owned. The Definitive Agreement should provide that improvements and derivatives of Stellarion Background IP (including EdgeAI) vest solely in Stellarion, and of Helix Background IP solely in Helix, with the remainder of Meridian output jointly owned.",
 ],
 position="Restore the Term Sheet scope (all IP arising from Project Meridian), subject to a carve-out that improvements, modifications and derivatives of either party's Background IP are owned by that party (with a license back to the other party for Meridian purposes only)."),

dict(id="D-26", area="D. Project Meridian Co-Development",
 title="New Joint IP prosecution cooperation and equal (50/50) sharing of filing and prosecution costs; vesting cooperation",
 ref="TS — / EL §6.3",
 ts="Silent.",
 el="Parties cooperate in filing, prosecution and maintenance of Joint IP patents and share reasonable costs equally; each party executes instruments to vest joint ownership.",
 sev="Minor", favors="Neutral", action="Accept",
 analysis=["Reasonable gap-filler. Consider (i) who controls prosecution (Stellarion, as the patent-focused party, should lead), (ii) a right for either party to take over prosecution of an application the other declines to fund, and (iii) enforcement and joinder rules (under U.S. patent law both co-owners generally must join an infringement suit)."],
 position="Accept, adding prosecution control, step-in and enforcement provisions in the Definitive Agreement."),

# ---------------- E. BACKGROUND IP ----------------
dict(id="D-27", area="E. Background IP",
 title="\"Background IP\" redefined: includes IP \"licensed to\" a party; measured at Engagement Letter date; independently developed IP excluded if it uses any of the other party's Confidential Information or \"resources\"",
 ref="TS §6 / EL §3 (\"Background IP\"), §7",
 ts="All pre-existing IP of each party, and IP \"developed by [the party] prior to or independently of the co-development activities,\" remains that party's sole property.",
 el="Background IP = IP \"owned by or licensed to a Party as of the Effective Date, or developed or acquired by a Party independently of this Agreement and without use of the other Party's Confidential Information or resources.\" Ownership language in §7 otherwise tracks the Term Sheet and adds \"by implication, estoppel, or otherwise.\"",
 sev="Moderate", favors="Mixed", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=[
  "(i) \"Licensed to\": Background IP is the trigger for each party's indemnity (EL §9.1). Including in-licensed IP expands Stellarion's indemnity to third-party components embedded in EdgeAI (e.g., open source or commercial libraries), uncapped under EL §9.2 (D-35). (ii) The \"without use of ... resources\" test is vague; Helix could argue that EdgeAI improvements Stellarion develops while working on Meridian with Helix-provided test environments are not Stellarion Background IP. (iii) The added \"by implication, estoppel, or otherwise\" language helps Stellarion and should be kept.",
 ],
 position="Define Stellarion Background IP to include EdgeAI and all improvements, modifications and derivatives of it however and whenever developed; delete \"or resources\"; and decouple the indemnity trigger from in-licensed IP (indemnity limited to EdgeAI as delivered, with customary exclusions; see D-37)."),

dict(id="D-28", area="E. Background IP",
 title="New royalty-free cross-license of each party's Background IP to perform Project Meridian",
 ref="TS — / EL §7 (third paragraph)",
 ts="No Background IP license for co-development (the EdgeAI license itself is royalty-bearing and field-limited).",
 el="Each party grants the other \"a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, royalty-free license to use such Party's Background IP solely to the extent necessary ... to perform its obligations under Project Meridian,\" terminating on completion of Meridian or termination of the Agreement.",
 sev="Moderate", favors="Helix", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=[
  "A performance license is reasonable in principle, but as drafted it gives Helix a royalty-free right to use all Stellarion Background IP (including all 14 patents, 7 applications and EdgeAI trade secrets) without the field-of-use limit, without an express no-sublicense rule (it is only \"non-transferable\"), and without confidentiality conditions. It does not address what rights Helix has in Stellarion Background IP to commercialize Meridian afterward; Helix may argue that the right to \"exploit, use, license\" Joint IP (EL §6.3) carries an implied license to the EdgeAI technology needed to practice it.",
 ],
 position="Limit to internal use for Project Meridian development only, within the Licensed Field, non-sublicensable (other than to approved subcontractors bound by confidentiality), subject to EL §10; and state expressly that any commercial exploitation of Meridian that incorporates or requires Stellarion Background IP requires (and is subject to the field, royalty and sublicensing terms of) the EdgeAI license."),

# ---------------- F. NONCOMPETE / EXCLUSIVITY / MFN ----------------
dict(id="D-29", area="F. Non-Compete, Exclusivity and MFN",
 title="Non-compete post-termination period cut from 18 to 12 months",
 ref="TS §7 / EL §8.1",
 ts="During the license term and 18 months after expiration or termination (the Restricted Period).",

The 18-month tail was a negotiated element of the package in which Stellarion conceded the MFN (see Part IV.3); Helix appears to have kept the reduced restriction while dropping its own consideration-side term, which suggests the package may have been deliberately re-cut."],

dict(id="D-30", area="F. Non-Compete, Exclusivity and MFN",
 title="Non-compete scope narrowed: \"otherwise exploit\" and \"in collaboration with any third party\" deleted; new carve-out for third-party components that are not a \"standalone\" ML inference engine",
 ref="TS §7 / EL §8.1",
 ts="Helix shall not \"develop, market, license, or otherwise exploit\" a competing ML inference engine for edge computing, \"whether independently or in collaboration with any third party\"; restriction applies to \"standalone or embedded ML inference engine technology that would be a functional substitute\" for EdgeAI.",
 el="Helix shall not \"develop, market, distribute, or license (or engage any third party to develop on its behalf)\" a competing engine. New: use of third-party components that provide \"ancillary analytics or data processing functions but do not constitute a standalone ML inference engine\" is not a breach.",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=[
  "Three loopholes: (i) deleting \"otherwise exploit\" removes, among other things, Helix's own use and deployment of a competing engine (including in hosted services) and investment in or acquisition of a competing engine business; (ii) replacing \"in collaboration with any third party\" with \"engage any third party to develop on its behalf\" permits joint ventures, co-development partnerships and reseller or OEM arrangements in which the third party, not Helix, owns the competing engine; and (iii) the new \"standalone\" carve-out inverts the Term Sheet, which expressly covered \"standalone or embedded\" engines. Under the Engagement Letter, Helix could embed a third-party inference capability inside Helix Edge Runtime and argue it is merely an \"ancillary\" component that is not \"standalone.\"",
 ],
 position="Restore the Term Sheet operative language (\"develop, market, license, distribute, use, deploy or otherwise exploit ... whether independently or in collaboration with any third party\" and \"standalone or embedded\"). If any carve-out is accepted, limit it to third-party components that do not perform machine learning inference and are not a functional substitute for any EdgeAI function."),

dict(id="D-31", area="F. Non-Compete, Exclusivity and MFN",
 title="Non-compete omitted from the express survival list",
 ref="TS §12.3(d) / EL §11.3",
 ts="\"the non-compete obligation set forth in Section 7 shall survive for the Restricted Period specified therein.\"",
 el="Survival list covers §§3, 5 (accrued payments), 7, 9, 9.2, 10, 15 and 16. Section 8 is not listed.",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=[
  "Although EL §8.1 itself refers to a post-termination period, an express survival clause that lists specific sections invites the argument (expressio unius) that unlisted provisions, including §8.1, do not survive termination. A post-term restriction whose survival is disputed is worth much less. This is either a drafting oversight or a deliberate omission; either way it must be fixed.",
 ],
 position="Add \"Section 8.1 (Helix Non-Compete), for the Non-Compete Period\" to the survival list (see also D-46 for other omissions)."),

dict(id="D-32", area="F. Non-Compete, Exclusivity and MFN",
 title="Stellarion exclusivity period shortened from 24 to 18 months",

 sev="Minor", favors="Stellarion", action="Accept",
 analysis=[
  "This reduces Stellarion's restriction and is Stellarion-favorable; we recommend accepting it. Note that (i) because the Effective Date is moved earlier (D-2), the 18 months begin at Engagement Letter signing, ending sooner still; (ii) the Term Sheet exclusivity is a Binding Provision that the Engagement Letter would supersede; and (iii) if the MFN is reinstated with the Term Sheet's link to \"the exclusivity period\" (see D-34), the MFN window would also be 18 months. Helix may notice this and seek to revert to 24 months; if so, 24 months is the Term Sheet position and should not be resisted strongly.",
 ],
 position="Accept 18 months; do not spend leverage defending it."),

dict(id="D-33", area="F. Non-Compete, Exclusivity and MFN",

 ts="Schedule to be negotiated in good faith and \"finalized prior to execution of the Definitive Agreement\"; Stellarion free to license to \"any party not listed\" on the schedule.",
 el="Schedule A \"shall be negotiated and finalized ... as part of the Definitive Agreement\"; pending finalization, parties cooperate in good faith to identify direct competitors; Stellarion free to license to \"any Person that is not a direct competitor of Helix.\" Schedule A is referenced as attached \"hereto\" but is not attached.",

The Term Sheet's \"not listed\" safe harbor was a clear bright line; the Engagement Letter replaces it with a standard that clouds Stellarion's freedom to license EdgeAI during the interim period.",
 ],

# ---------------- G. INDEMNITY / LOL ----------------
dict(id="D-35", area="G. Indemnification and Limitation of Liability",
 title="Indemnification obligations carved OUT of the liability cap (uncapped), reversing the Term Sheet's express statement that indemnity is within the cap",
 ref="TS §10, §11 / EL §9.2",
 ts="\"For the avoidance of doubt, indemnification obligations under Section 10 are subject to and included within the aggregate liability cap.\" Only exclusions: confidentiality breaches; willful misconduct or fraud.",
 el="Cap does not apply to \"(A) a Party's indemnification obligations under Section 9.1,\" confidentiality breaches, or willful misconduct/fraud. The consequential-damages waiver also does not apply to these carve-outs.",
 sev="Dealbreaker", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=[
  "The indemnity is mutual in form but asymmetric in substance: Stellarion is the party contributing the core licensed IP, which Helix will distribute worldwide to a base of approximately 3,400 enterprise customers, so Stellarion's IP indemnity is the obligation most likely to be called. Removing it from the cap, and from the consequential-damages waiver, exposes Stellarion to unlimited liability, including customers' consequential damages passed through as \"third-party claims\", in exchange for a $12.5 million upfront fee. For a company with $67.3 million ARR, a single significant patent assertion against Helix's installed base could exceed Stellarion's total consideration under the deal and threaten solvency.",
  "The Term Sheet language was explicit (\"for the avoidance of doubt ... included within\"), so this is a direct reversal of a negotiated point, not a gap-fill.",
 ],
 position="Reject. Restore: indemnification obligations are subject to and included within the aggregate cap. If Helix insists on separate treatment, the most Stellarion should consider is a separate IP indemnity super-cap (e.g., the greater of fees paid in the prior 24 months or a fixed amount not exceeding the $25 million general cap), with customary exclusions and remedies (see D-37)."),

dict(id="D-36", area="G. Indemnification and Limitation of Liability",
 title="Aggregate liability cap reduced from $25,000,000 to $20,000,000",
 ref="TS §11 / EL §9.2",
 ts="$25,000,000 aggregate cap per party.",
 el="$20,000,000 aggregate cap per party.",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=[
  "With indemnity carved out (D-35), a lower cap principally limits what Stellarion can recover from Helix, for example for Helix's misuse of EdgeAI outside the field, breach of the non-compete, unauthorized sublicensing, or non-payment, while Stellarion's own largest exposure (indemnity) is uncapped. The combination is doubly adverse. Note also that, as drafted, Helix's unpaid fees and royalties could themselves count toward the cap.",
 ],
 position="Restore $25,000,000 and add an express carve-out so that Helix's payment obligations (upfront fee, royalties, minimum royalty) are not limited by or counted toward the cap."),

dict(id="D-37", area="G. Indemnification and Limitation of Liability",
 title="Indemnity scope broadened (\"infringes, misappropriates, or otherwise violates\"; \"arising out of or relating to\"; successors and assigns) without customary IP indemnity exclusions or remedies",
 ref="TS §10 / EL §9.1",
 ts="Indemnity for third-party claims \"arising from alleged infringement of intellectual property rights by the indemnifying party's Background IP\"; procedures to be detailed in the Definitive Agreement; subject to the cap.",
 el="Indemnity for Losses \"arising out of or relating to any claim that the Indemnifying Party's Background IP, as contributed to or utilized in the arrangement ... infringes, misappropriates, or otherwise violates\" third-party IP; Indemnified Parties include successors and assigns. No exclusions; no mitigation remedies.",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=[
  "Adding misappropriation and \"otherwise violates\" (trade secret, moral rights, etc.) broadens Stellarion's exposure beyond infringement. \"As ... utilized in the arrangement\" extends coverage to EdgeAI as integrated, modified and combined by Helix. The letter omits the standard licensor protections: no indemnity for claims caused by (a) Helix modifications (Helix has a modification right under EL §4.1), (b) combination with Helix Edge Runtime or other non-Stellarion technology where the claim would not arise but for the combination, (c) use outside the Licensed Field or in breach of the Agreement, (d) continued use after Stellarion provides a non-infringing update; and no right for Stellarion to procure a license, modify or replace, or terminate and refund as its sole obligation. Including \"successors and assigns\" matters given the free M&A assignment right (D-54).",
 ],
 position="Limit to infringement or misappropriation by EdgeAI as delivered by Stellarion and used in accordance with the Agreement; add the customary exclusions and remedies (procure/modify/replace/terminate); keep within the cap (D-35)."),

dict(id="D-38", area="G. Indemnification and Limitation of Liability",
 title="Indemnification procedures added (prompt notice with prejudice standard; control of defense; settlement consent)",
 ref="TS §10 (procedures to Definitive Agreement) / EL §9.1",
 ts="Standard procedures to be set out in the Definitive Agreement.",
 el="Prompt notice (failure excuses only to the extent of material prejudice); indemnitor controls defense with counsel reasonably acceptable to indemnitee; indemnitee \"shall cooperate fully\"; no settlement imposing obligations or lacking full release without consent.",
 sev="Minor", favors="Neutral", action="Accept",
 analysis=["Market-standard and mutual. Minor refinements: cooperation should be at the indemnitor's expense; indemnitor's control should not be conditioned on counsel being \"reasonably acceptable\" (or the standard should be stated objectively)."],
 position="Accept with minor refinements."),

dict(id="D-39", area="G. Indemnification and Limitation of Liability",
 title="Consequential damages waiver expressly includes lost profits and revenue, with no carve-out for license-scope, field-of-use, non-compete, sublicensing or payment breaches",
 ref="TS §11 / EL §9.2 (second paragraph)",
 ts="Mutual waiver of indirect, incidental, consequential, special or punitive damages. Exclusions from the cap: confidentiality; willful misconduct or fraud.",
 el="Waiver expanded to \"exemplary\" damages and expressly to \"loss of profits, loss of revenue, loss of data, loss of business opportunity, or loss of goodwill\"; excepted only for the cap carve-outs (indemnity, confidentiality, willful misconduct/fraud).",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=[
  "Stellarion's principal damages if Helix deploys EdgeAI in supply chain optimization, breaches the non-compete, or sublicenses without consent would be lost profits in its core market. The Engagement Letter's express inclusion of lost profits and lost business opportunity in the waiver would bar most of that recovery, leaving Stellarion with injunctive relief (which, under the exclusive arbitration clause, is itself uncertain; see D-53). The Term Sheet waiver had the same basic architecture, so part of this is a gap common to both documents; but the express listing of lost profits makes the Engagement Letter materially worse.",
 ],
 position="Carve out from both the cap and the consequential damages waiver: (i) Helix's use of EdgeAI or Joint IP outside the scope of the license (including the Excluded Field), (ii) breach of the non-compete and sublicensing restrictions, (iii) infringement or misappropriation of the other party's IP, and (iv) payment obligations. At a minimum, delete the express reference to lost profits/revenue for these categories."),

# ---------------- H. CONFIDENTIALITY ----------------
dict(id="D-40", area="H. Confidentiality",
 title="Confidentiality survival cut from 3 years to 2 years",
 ref="TS §14 (Binding) / EL §10.2",
 ts="Survives three years after expiration or termination of the Definitive Agreement.",
 el="Survives two years after expiration or termination of \"this Agreement.\"",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=[
  "Helix will receive EdgeAI technical information (and, in the interim, potentially escrow-related materials) and will co-develop with Stellarion's engineers. A two-year tail is short for trade secrets in transformer-based ML architectures, and losing trade-secret status by contract is a real risk because confidentiality obligations that expire can undercut the \"reasonable measures\" element of trade secret protection. Note also that the clock runs from termination of the Engagement Letter, which could end soon (e.g., when superseded or terminated on 60 days' notice).",
 ],
 position="Restore three years minimum; add that obligations for trade secrets and source code continue for as long as the information remains a trade secret under applicable law; and clarify that supersession of the Engagement Letter by the Definitive Agreement does not end the tail."),

dict(id="D-41", area="H. Confidentiality",
 title="\"Confidential Information\" narrowed (designated or reasonably understood as confidential); exceptions loosened; permitted recipients expanded to consultants and contractors",
 ref="TS §14 / EL §3 (\"Confidential Information\"), §10.1",
 ts="All non-public technical, business, financial and other information disclosed in connection with the transactions, in any form. Prior-knowledge exception requires evidence by written records; public-domain exception requires no breach by the recipient. Disclosure permitted to employees, directors, advisors and professional representatives with need to know.",
 el="Information \"designated as confidential or that ... reasonably should be understood to be confidential\"; prior-knowledge exception without written-records requirement; public-domain exception \"through no fault\"; disclosure permitted also to \"officers, ... consultants, and contractors\" bound by written obligations; compelled-disclosure exception added; terms of the Agreement expressly confidential.",
 sev="Moderate", favors="Mixed (net Helix)", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=[
  "The marking/reasonable-understanding test is common but narrower than the Term Sheet's \"all non-public information\" formulation and shifts the burden to Stellarion in a dispute. Dropping the written-records evidentiary requirement makes the prior-knowledge exception easier for Helix to invoke against EdgeAI information. Permitting disclosure to \"consultants and contractors\" lets EdgeAI information reach third parties (potentially including contractors who also work for Stellarion competitors) on a need-to-know basis. On the other side, the compelled-disclosure exception, the express treatment of agreement terms as confidential, and the written-obligation requirement for recipients are acceptable or favorable.",
 ],
 position="Restore the Term Sheet's broad definition (or deem all EdgeAI technical information, source code and Stellarion product roadmaps confidential regardless of marking); restore the written-records requirement; permit disclosure to contractors only with Stellarion's prior consent for EdgeAI technical information; keep the compelled-disclosure exception; make each party liable for its recipients."),

dict(id="D-42", area="H. Confidentiality",
 title="New use restriction, standard of care and return/destruction obligations (with one archival copy)",
 ref="TS §14 / EL §10.1",
 ts="Non-disclosure only; no express use restriction.",
 el="No use except to perform obligations or exercise rights; at least the same degree of care as for own information (no less than reasonable); return or destroy at discloser's election, with certification; one archival copy for legal/compliance purposes.",
 sev="Minor", favors="Stellarion", action="Accept",

# ---------------- I. TERMINATION ----------------
dict(id="D-43", area="I. Termination",
 title="Breach termination: 30-day notice running concurrently with 30-day cure (effective approximately 30 days) instead of 60-day notice and 30-day cure (90 days total); \"material breach ... of any material provision\"",
 ref="TS §12.1 / EL §11.1",
 ts="60 days' written notice; 30-day cure period; termination effective on expiry of cure period, \"i.e., ninety (90) days total from delivery of the initial notice of breach.\"",
 el="Termination on 30 days' prior written notice for \"a material breach ... of any material provision,\" if the breach remains uncured 30 days after receipt of notice.",
 sev="Moderate", favors="Mixed", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=[
  "The Engagement Letter compresses the termination timeline from about 90 days to about 30. Because the right is mutual, the effect cuts both ways: it lets Stellarion terminate faster for Helix's breach (e.g., non-payment, field-of-use violations), but it also exposes Stellarion to rapid termination by Helix (for example, over a Meridian performance dispute) shortly after Stellarion has deposited source code and committed development resources. The double materiality qualifier (\"material breach\" of a \"material provision\") raises the bar for terminating and is generally unhelpful to the licensor.",
  "Term Sheet drafting note: TS §12.1 is internally inconsistent: a 30-day cure period running \"following receipt of such notice\" would expire on day 30, not day 90. The parenthetical shows the intended reading (60-day notice period followed by 30-day cure); the Definitive Agreement should state the mechanics unambiguously.",
 ],
 position="Negotiate a split regime: (i) payment defaults: 15–30 day cure, then immediate termination; (ii) breaches of the field-of-use, sublicensing, confidentiality or non-compete provisions: termination on 30 days' notice if uncured (or immediately if not curable or willful); (iii) all other material breaches: the Term Sheet's 90-day framework. Delete \"of any material provision.\""),

dict(id="D-44", area="I. Termination",
 title="Insolvency termination: 60-day dismissal window for involuntary petitions; \"general\" assignment; \"all or a substantial portion\" of assets",
 ref="TS §12.2 / EL §11.2",
 ts="Immediate termination on insolvency, bankruptcy petition (voluntary or involuntary), assignment for benefit of creditors, or receiver for substantially all assets.",
 el="Same triggers, but involuntary petitions count only if not dismissed within 60 days; receiver trigger extends to \"all or a substantial portion\" of assets.",
 sev="Minor", favors="Neutral", action="Accept",
 analysis=["Market-standard refinements, mutual in effect. Note that ipso facto termination rights may be unenforceable against a debtor under the U.S. Bankruptcy Code, and Helix as licensee would have rights under 11 U.S.C. §365(n) if Stellarion were the debtor; neither point is a reason to reject the clause."],
 position="Accept."),

dict(id="D-45", area="I. Termination",
 title="New 90-day Wind-Down Period on any expiration or termination (including for Helix's breach); royalties on wind-down sales not addressed",
 ref="TS §12.3(a), (b) / EL §11.3",
 ts="License terminates \"subject to any wind-down period to be agreed upon in the Definitive Agreement\"; Helix \"shall immediately cease\" all use, reproduction and distribution.",
 el="Helix must cease use within 90 days; during the Wind-Down Period it may continue to distribute to fulfil orders accepted before termination. Applies to termination \"for any reason.\"",
 sev="Moderate", favors="Helix", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=[
  "A 90-day wind-down is not unusual, but (i) it applies even where Stellarion terminates for Helix's breach, including field-of-use or sublicensing violations; (ii) running royalties are payable \"during the License Term\" (EL §5.2), so Helix may argue no royalty is owed on wind-down sales after the License Term ends; and (iii) existing customer deployments are not addressed (perpetual end-user rights would need Stellarion's agreement).",
 ],
 position="Wind-down only for expiration or termination other than for Helix's breach; royalties expressly payable on all wind-down revenue; no new customers during wind-down; wind-down rights subject to all license restrictions including the Excluded Field."),

dict(id="D-46", area="I. Termination",
 title="Survival list omits Joint IP ownership/sublicensing (§6.3), reservation of rights (§4.3), escrow post-release license limits (§12) and wind-down terms; lists §9 and §9.2 redundantly",

 ts="Accrued payments, non-compete and confidentiality survive.",
 el="Survival of §§3, 5 (accrued payments only), 7, 9, 9.2, 10 (subject to §10.2), 15, 16.",
 sev="Moderate", favors="Ambiguous", action="Negotiate",

dict(id="D-48", area="J. Source Code Escrow",

dict(id="D-49", area="J. Source Code Escrow",

# ---------------- K. REPS ----------------
dict(id="D-50", area="K. Representations and Warranties",
 title="New representations and warranties (including Stellarion's sole-ownership, knowledge-qualified non-infringement and no-claims representations) and disclaimer",
 ref="TS §16 (reps to Definitive Agreement) / EL §13",
 ts="Representations and warranties to be included in the Definitive Agreement.",
 el="Mutual organizational and authority reps; Stellarion: sole owner of EdgeAI free and clear of liens; to its knowledge non-infringing; no pending or (to its knowledge) threatened claims; full right to grant licenses. Helix: owns Helix Edge Runtime; to its knowledge non-infringing; has resources for Meridian. Broad disclaimer.",
 sev="Moderate", favors="Helix (asymmetric)", action="Flag for further discussion",
 analysis=[
  "The Stellarion representations are not unreasonable in principle, but they are given now (in an interim letter) and are asymmetric: Helix gives no \"no pending claims\" or \"full right\" representation. Before signing, Stellarion should confirm: (i) no lender liens or security interests over its IP (a \"free and clear\" representation is breached by a routine IP security interest under a credit facility); (ii) the open-source and third-party components in EdgeAI (\"sole and exclusive owner of all right, title, and interest\" is inaccurate if EdgeAI incorporates licensed components); (iii) that no existing license, exclusivity or MFN granted to another party conflicts with the Helix grant (mutual rep 13.1(d)). The disclaimer is helpful to Stellarion and should be kept.",
 ],
 position="Move substantive IP representations to the Definitive Agreement; if given now, qualify by a disclosure schedule, limit \"sole owner\" to Stellarion-developed components and disclose liens and open source; make the no-claims representation mutual."),

# ---------------- N. GENERAL ----------------
dict(id="D-54", area="N. General Provisions",
 title="Assignment: consent \"not unreasonably withheld\" and free assignment without consent in a merger, consolidation, reorganization or sale of substantially all assets",
 ref="TS §18 (No Assignment) / EL §16.2",
 ts="No assignment without the prior written consent of the other party; non-consensual assignment void.",
 el="Consent not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed; either party may assign without consent in connection with a merger, consolidation, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all assets, if the assignee agrees to be bound.",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=[
  "The M&A exception lets Helix transfer the EdgeAI license, its Joint IP rights and its escrow rights to an acquirer without Stellarion's consent, including a Stellarion competitor in supply chain analytics or an ML inference vendor, and Change of control of Helix (e.g., a stock acquisition) is not addressed at all.  ],
