 analysis=["Doubling the threshold lets Helix under-report by up to just under 10% with no consequence beyond paying the shortfall, weakening the deterrent value of the audit right at the very point (bundled revenue allocations, D-12) where deterrence matters most."],
 position="Restore 5%."),

dict(id="D-18", area="C. Financial Terms",
 title="Audit mechanics: nationally recognized firm; on-site at Helix; 1.5% per month interest; records retained 3 years after each Royalty Year; Affiliates not covered",
 ref="TS §4.4 / EL §5.4",
 ts="Independent CPA selected by Stellarion and reasonably acceptable to Helix; interest at the rate in the Definitive Agreement; records for at least 3 years after the applicable royalty period.",
 el="“Independent, nationally recognized accounting firm reasonably acceptable to Helix”; at Helix’s principal offices; interest at the lesser of 1.5% per month or the legal maximum from the original due date; records for 3 years after the end of the applicable Royalty Year.",
 sev="Minor", favors="Mixed", action="Accept",
 analysis=["The fixed interest rate favors Stellarion; retention is equal or slightly longer. “Nationally recognized” narrows the auditor pool modestly. Gaps: the audit right covers only Helix’s books although Gross Revenue includes Affiliate revenue, and because “Royalty Year” begins only in Year 2, retention for Year 1 records is ambiguous."],
 position="Accept, extending audit to Affiliates and running retention from the end of each calendar year (including Year 1)."),

dict(id="D-19", area="C. Financial Terms",
 title="No general late-payment interest or remedy for late fees and royalties",
 ref="TS §4.4 / EL §5",
 ts="Interest on audit underpayments at a rate to be specified in the Definitive Agreement.",
 el="Interest only on audit-revealed underpayments; none on late upfront installments, royalties or minimum shortfalls.",
 sev="Minor", favors="Helix", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=["A gap rather than a deviation, but it matters given the longer payment windows in D-11, D-13 and D-16."],
 position="Add interest at 1.5% per month (or the legal maximum, if lower) on all overdue amounts, and a right to suspend Helix’s distribution rights after 30 days of uncured non-payment."),

dict(id="D-20", area="D. Project Meridian Co-Development",
 title="New Steering Committee with authority to set milestones, approve work plans, allocate resources and resolve disputes; no voting or deadlock mechanism",
 ref="TS §5.1 / EL §6.1",
 ts="Joint development plan (specifications, milestones, staffing, acceptance criteria) to be set out in the Definitive Agreement or a statement of work; integration into Helix Edge Runtime “and potentially other authorized products as mutually agreed.”",
 el="Equal-representation Steering Committee responsible for “setting milestones, approving work plans, allocating resources, and resolving any disputes.” Reference to other authorized products omitted.",
 sev="Moderate", favors="Neutral / ambiguous", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=["A steering committee is customary, but as drafted (i) “allocating resources” could be read to let the committee commit Stellarion personnel and spending, which with the uncapped overrun rule (D-22) creates open-ended exposure; (ii) there is no voting rule or deadlock-breaker; and (iii) committee “dispute resolution” sits uneasily with exclusive arbitration (EL §15.2)."],
 position="Accept a Steering Committee with unanimous decisions; no authority to amend the Agreement, raise the budget or commit resources beyond the approved plan; escalation to the CEOs within 15 business days, then arbitration; no power to waive field, sublicensing or IP provisions."),

dict(id="D-21", area="D. Project Meridian Co-Development",
 title="Cost split changed from 60% Helix / 40% Stellarion to 55% Helix / 45% Stellarion",
 ref="TS §5.2 / EL §6.2",
 ts="$8,200,000 budget: Helix 60% ($4,920,000); Stellarion 40% ($3,280,000).",
 el="$8,200,000 budget: Helix 55% ($4,510,000); Stellarion 45% ($3,690,000).",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=["Shifts $410,000 of budgeted cost to Stellarion (a 12.5% increase in Stellarion’s share), and the same 45% ratio applies to every overrun dollar (D-22). The Engagement Letter arithmetic is internally correct."],
 position="Restore 60/40 ($4,920,000 / $3,280,000)."),

dict(id="D-22", area="D. Project Meridian Co-Development",
 title="Cost overruns shared automatically pro rata; Term Sheet requirement of mutual written approval for overruns above 10% deleted",
 ref="TS §5.2 / EL §6.2",
 ts="“Any cost overruns exceeding ten percent (10%) of the estimated budget shall require mutual written approval of both parties before such overruns are incurred.”",
 el="“Costs incurred in excess of the Project Budget shall be allocated between the Parties in the same proportion … (i.e., 55% to Helix and 45% to Stellarion), unless otherwise agreed by the Parties in writing.”",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=["Removes Stellarion’s veto over budget growth and makes its exposure uncapped. Illustration: a 25% overrun ($2,050,000) would cost Stellarion $922,500 under the Engagement Letter with no approval right; under the Term Sheet the overrun could not be incurred without Stellarion’s prior written approval (and would be shared 40%, $820,000, only if approved). With the Steering Committee’s resource authority (D-20) and the invoicing mechanics (D-23), Helix could drive spending Stellarion must fund."],
 position="Restore the Term Sheet rule: no overrun above 10% of the budget may be incurred as a shared cost without both parties’ prior written approval; overruns within the 10% band shared 60/40."),

dict(id="D-23", area="D. Project Meridian Co-Development",
 title="Rule that each party bears its own personnel costs omitted; reciprocal quarterly invoicing for “costs incurred” (shared cost pool undefined)",
 ref="TS §5.2 / EL §6.2",
 ts="Each party bears its own personnel costs (salaries, benefits, overhead); only shared costs (third-party tools, cloud infrastructure, testing services) are split; quarterly allocation per the plan.",
 el="Each party invoices the other quarterly “for the other Party’s share of costs incurred during the preceding quarter,” payable within 30 days. No personnel cost rule.",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=["Without the personnel cost rule, either party can treat its internal engineering salaries, benefits and overhead as “costs incurred” and invoice the other for its percentage. Helix, with roughly $1.2 billion in revenue and a far larger organization, is better placed to load costs (including overhead allocations) into the pool. The Term Sheet deliberately limited cross-charging to genuine third-party shared costs."],
 position="Restore: “Each Party shall bear its own personnel costs (including salaries, benefits and overhead). Only Shared Costs (third-party tools, cloud infrastructure and testing services, incurred under the approved plan and supported by third-party invoices) shall be allocated 60% to Helix and 40% to Stellarion.” Add audit rights over shared cost invoices."),

dict(id="D-24", area="D. Project Meridian Co-Development",
 title="JOINT IP SUBLICENSING: prior written consent requirement deleted; each party may “license” Joint IP without consent [GC PRIORITY 2]",
 ref="TS §5.3 / EL §6.3",
 ts="Each party may exploit Co-Developed IP without consent or accounting, “subject to the restriction set forth below. However, neither party may sublicense jointly-owned Co-Developed IP to any third party without the prior written consent of the other party.” Consent not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed.",
 el="“Each Party shall have the right to exploit, use, license, and otherwise commercialize the Joint IP without the consent of, or any obligation to account to, the other Party.” No sublicensing restriction.",
 sev="Dealbreaker", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=["See Part IV.2 for the full analysis."],
 position="Reject and restore the Term Sheet consent requirement, extended to all forms of licensing (Part IV.2; Appendix A-2)."),

dict(id="D-25", area="D. Project Meridian Co-Development",
 title="“Joint IP” narrowed to IP jointly created by both parties’ personnel; Meridian IP created by one party alone falls outside joint ownership",
 ref="TS §5.3 (“Co-Developed IP”) / EL §3 (“Joint IP”), §6.3",
 ts="“All intellectual property arising from Project Meridian, including all inventions, discoveries, improvements, works of authorship, software, algorithms, and related documentation” is jointly owned.",
 el="Joint IP is IP “conceived, created, developed, or reduced to practice jointly by employees or contractors of both Parties in the course of, and arising from, Project Meridian.” No rule for IP created by one party alone.",
 sev="Material", favors="Ambiguous (likely Helix)", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=[
  "Under the Term Sheet everything arising from Project Meridian is joint; under the Engagement Letter only jointly-created IP is joint, and Meridian work product created by one party’s team alone would by default belong to the creating party. Helix is likely to perform most of the integration engineering on Helix Edge Runtime, so this gap could leave Helix as sole owner of significant Meridian deliverables, free of any sublicensing restriction at all.",
  "The narrower definition also interacts with the Background IP boundary (D-27): EdgeAI improvements Stellarion makes alone during Meridian fall outside Joint IP (good for Stellarion) but may also fall outside Stellarion Background IP if any Helix “resources” were used.",
  "A related gap exists in both documents: neither carves out improvements to, or derivatives of, a party’s Background IP from co-developed IP. Under the Term Sheet’s broad definition, improvements to EdgeAI arising from Meridian would be jointly owned. The Definitive Agreement should provide that improvements and derivatives of Stellarion Background IP (including EdgeAI) vest solely in Stellarion, and of Helix Background IP solely in Helix, with the rest of the Meridian output jointly owned.",
 ],
 position="Restore the Term Sheet scope (all IP arising from Project Meridian), subject to a carve-out that improvements, modifications and derivatives of a party’s Background IP belong to that party, with a license back for Meridian purposes only."),

dict(id="D-26", area="D. Project Meridian Co-Development",
 title="New Joint IP prosecution cooperation, vesting cooperation and equal (50/50) sharing of filing and prosecution costs",
 ref="TS — / EL §6.3",
 ts="Silent.",
 el="Parties cooperate in filing, prosecution and maintenance of Joint IP patents and share reasonable costs equally; each executes instruments to vest joint ownership.",
 sev="Minor", favors="Neutral", action="Accept",
 analysis=["Reasonable gap-filler. Address in the Definitive Agreement: who controls prosecution (Stellarion, as the patent-focused party, should lead); a step-in right if one party declines to fund an application; and enforcement and joinder (in the U.S. all patent co-owners generally must join an infringement suit)."],
 position="Accept, adding prosecution control, step-in and enforcement terms in the Definitive Agreement."),

dict(id="D-27", area="E. Background IP",
 title="“Background IP” redefined: includes IP “licensed to” a party; measured at the Engagement Letter date; independently developed IP excluded if it uses any of the other party’s Confidential Information or “resources”",
 ref="TS §6 / EL §3 (“Background IP”), §7",
 ts="All pre-existing IP of each party, and IP developed by it “prior to or independently of the co-development activities,” remains that party’s sole property.",
 el="Background IP is IP “owned by or licensed to a Party as of the Effective Date, or developed or acquired by a Party independently of this Agreement and without use of the other Party’s Confidential Information or resources.” Ownership language in §7 otherwise tracks the Term Sheet and adds “by implication, estoppel, or otherwise.”",
 sev="Moderate", favors="Mixed", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=["(i) “Licensed to”: Background IP is the trigger for each party’s indemnity (EL §9.1), so including in-licensed IP expands Stellarion’s indemnity to third-party components in EdgeAI (open source or commercial libraries), uncapped under EL §9.2 (D-35). (ii) The “without use of … resources” test is vague; Helix could argue that EdgeAI improvements Stellarion develops using Helix-provided test environments are not Stellarion Background IP. (iii) The added “by implication, estoppel, or otherwise” language helps Stellarion and should be kept."],
 position="Define Stellarion Background IP to include EdgeAI and all improvements, modifications and derivatives of it however and whenever developed; delete “or resources”; decouple the indemnity trigger from in-licensed IP (D-37)."),

dict(id="D-28", area="E. Background IP",
 title="New royalty-free cross-license of each party’s Background IP to perform Project Meridian",
 ref="TS — / EL §7 (third paragraph)",
 ts="No Background IP license for co-development (the EdgeAI license itself is royalty-bearing and field-limited).",
 el="Each party grants the other “a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, royalty-free license to use such Party’s Background IP solely to the extent necessary … to perform its obligations under Project Meridian,” ending on completion of Meridian or termination.",
 sev="Moderate", favors="Helix", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=["A performance license is reasonable in principle, but as drafted it gives Helix a royalty-free right to use all Stellarion Background IP (including the 14 patents, 7 applications and EdgeAI trade secrets) without the field-of-use limit, without an express no-sublicense rule (it is only “non-transferable”), and without express confidentiality conditions. It is also silent on what rights Helix has in Stellarion Background IP to commercialize Meridian afterwards; Helix may argue that its right to “exploit, use, license” Joint IP (EL §6.3) carries an implied license to the EdgeAI technology needed to practice it."],
 position="Limit to internal development use for Project Meridian within the Licensed Field, non-sublicensable (other than to approved subcontractors bound by confidentiality), subject to EL §10; and state expressly that commercial exploitation of Meridian that incorporates or requires Stellarion Background IP requires, and is subject to the field, royalty and sublicensing terms of, the EdgeAI license."),

dict(id="D-29", area="F. Non-Compete, Exclusivity and MFN",
 title="Non-compete post-termination period cut from 18 to 12 months",
 ref="TS §7 / EL §8.1",
 ts="During the license term and 18 months after expiration or termination (the Restricted Period).",
 el="During the License Term and 12 months after expiration or termination (the Non-Compete Period).",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=["A one-third reduction in the post-term protection. The 18-month tail was part of the package in which Stellarion conceded the MFN (Part IV.3). Helix appears to have kept a reduced restriction while dropping the term that was its consideration, which suggests the package may have been deliberately re-cut."],
 position="Restore 18 months."),

dict(id="D-30", area="F. Non-Compete, Exclusivity and MFN",
 title="Non-compete scope narrowed: “otherwise exploit” and “in collaboration with any third party” deleted; new carve-out for third-party components that are not a “standalone” ML inference engine",
 ref="TS §7 / EL §8.1",
 ts="Helix shall not “develop, market, license, or otherwise exploit” a competing ML inference engine for edge computing, “whether independently or in collaboration with any third party”; the restriction covers “standalone or embedded ML inference engine technology that would be a functional substitute” for EdgeAI.",
 el="Helix shall not “develop, market, distribute, or license (or engage any third party to develop on its behalf)” a competing engine. New: use of third-party components that provide “ancillary analytics or data processing functions but do not constitute a standalone ML inference engine” is not a breach.",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=["Three loopholes: (i) deleting “otherwise exploit” removes Helix’s own use and deployment of a competing engine (including in hosted services) and investment in, or acquisition of, a competing engine business; (ii) replacing “in collaboration with any third party” with “engage any third party to develop on its behalf” permits joint ventures, co-development, reseller and OEM arrangements in which the third party owns the competing engine; (iii) the new “standalone” carve-out inverts the Term Sheet, which expressly covered “standalone or embedded” engines. Helix could embed a third-party inference capability inside Helix Edge Runtime and argue it is an “ancillary” component that is not “standalone.”"],
 position="Restore the Term Sheet operative language (“develop, market, license, distribute, use, deploy or otherwise exploit … whether independently or in collaboration with any third party”; “standalone or embedded”). Any carve-out should be limited to third-party components that do not perform machine learning inference and are not a functional substitute for any EdgeAI function."),

dict(id="D-31", area="F. Non-Compete, Exclusivity and MFN",
 title="Non-compete omitted from the express survival list",
 ref="TS §12.3(d) / EL §11.3",
 ts="“[T]he non-compete obligation set forth in Section 7 shall survive for the Restricted Period specified therein.”",
 el="Survival list covers §§3, 5 (accrued payments), 7, 9, 9.2, 10, 15 and 16. Section 8 is not listed.",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=["Although EL §8.1 refers to a post-termination period, an express survival clause listing specific sections invites the argument (expressio unius) that unlisted provisions, including §8.1, do not survive. A post-term restriction whose survival is disputed is worth much less. Whether oversight or deliberate, it must be fixed."],
 position="Add “Section 8.1 (Helix Non-Compete), for the Non-Compete Period” to the survival list (see also D-46)."),

dict(id="D-32", area="F. Non-Compete, Exclusivity and MFN",
 title="Stellarion exclusivity period shortened from 24 to 18 months",
 ref="TS §8 (Binding) / EL §8.2",
 ts="24 months from the Effective Date; a Binding Provision.",
 el="18 months from the Effective Date (now the Engagement Letter date).",
 sev="Minor", favors="Stellarion", action="Accept",
 analysis=["This shortens a restriction on Stellarion and is Stellarion-favorable. Notes: (i) because the Effective Date moves earlier (D-2), the 18 months also start sooner; (ii) the Term Sheet exclusivity is a Binding Provision that the Engagement Letter would supersede; (iii) if the MFN is reinstated with its Term Sheet link to “the exclusivity period” (D-34), the MFN window would also be 18 months. Helix may notice and ask to revert to 24 months; as that is the Term Sheet position, Stellarion should not resist it strongly."],
 position="Accept 18 months; do not spend leverage defending it."),

dict(id="D-33", area="F. Non-Compete, Exclusivity and MFN",
 title="Restricted Competitor Schedule (Schedule A) deferred to the Definitive Agreement; interim good faith identification; safe harbor shifts from “not listed” to “not a direct competitor”",
 ref="TS §8 / EL §8.2",
 ts="Schedule to be negotiated in good faith and “finalized prior to execution of the Definitive Agreement”; Stellarion free to license to “any party not listed” on the schedule.",
 el="Schedule A “shall be negotiated and finalized … as part of the Definitive Agreement”; pending finalization the parties cooperate in good faith to identify direct competitors; Stellarion free to license to “any Person that is not a direct competitor of Helix.” Schedule A is referred to as attached “hereto” but is not attached.",
 sev="Moderate", favors="Helix", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=["In the interim there is no list, so the restriction is either empty (no one is “listed on Schedule A”) or, as Helix will argue from the final sentence, applies to any “direct competitor of Helix,” an undefined and potentially broad category given Helix’s breadth (data lakes, streaming pipelines, edge compute). The Term Sheet’s “not listed” safe harbor was a bright line; the Engagement Letter clouds Stellarion’s freedom to license EdgeAI in the interim."],
 position="Attach an agreed Schedule A now (preferred), or state that until it is attached no Person is restricted; restore “not listed on Schedule A” as the safe harbor; cap the list (e.g., no more than eight to ten named entities, excluding their non-competing affiliates)."),

dict(id="D-34", area="F. Non-Compete, Exclusivity and MFN",
 title="MOST-FAVORED-NATION provision omitted entirely [GC PRIORITY 3]",
 ref="TS §9 / EL — (no corresponding provision)",
 ts="During the exclusivity period, if Stellarion licenses EdgeAI to a third party (other than Restricted Competitors) on terms more favorable “taken as a whole,” Stellarion must notify Helix and offer those terms; 30 days to elect; 30 days to implement.",
 el="No MFN provision. The supersession language (EL §1) and integration clause (EL §16.3) would extinguish TS §9.",
 sev="Material", favors="Stellarion on its face; creates risk", action="Flag for further discussion",
 analysis=["See Part IV.3 for the full analysis."],
 position="Flag for discussion. Our recommendation is to reinstate the Term Sheet MFN in its narrow form, expressly tied as consideration to a restored 18-month non-compete (Part IV.3; Appendix A-3)."),

dict(id="D-35", area="G. Indemnification and Limitation of Liability",
 title="Indemnification carved OUT of the liability cap (uncapped), reversing the Term Sheet’s express statement that indemnity is within the cap",
 ref="TS §10, §11 / EL §9.2",
 ts="“For the avoidance of doubt, indemnification obligations under Section 10 are subject to and included within the aggregate liability cap.” Only exclusions: confidentiality breaches; willful misconduct or fraud.",
 el="Cap does not apply to “(A) a Party’s indemnification obligations under Section 9.1,” confidentiality breaches, or willful misconduct or fraud. The consequential damages waiver also does not apply to these carve-outs.",
 sev="Dealbreaker", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=[
  "The indemnity is mutual in form but asymmetric in substance. Stellarion contributes the core licensed technology, which Helix will distribute worldwide across roughly 3,400 enterprise customers, so Stellarion’s IP indemnity is the obligation most likely to be called. Removing it from the cap and from the consequential damages waiver exposes Stellarion to unlimited liability, including customers’ consequential losses passed through as third-party claims, in exchange for a $12.5 million upfront fee. For a company with $67.3 million ARR, a single significant patent assertion against Helix’s installed base could exceed Stellarion’s total consideration under the deal.",
  "The Term Sheet language was explicit (“for the avoidance of doubt … included within”), so this is a direct reversal of a negotiated point, not a gap-fill.",
 ],
 position="Reject. Restore: indemnification obligations are subject to and included within the aggregate cap. If Helix insists on separate treatment, at most consider a separate IP indemnity super-cap no higher than the $25 million general cap, with customary exclusions and remedies (D-37)."),

dict(id="D-36", area="G. Indemnification and Limitation of Liability",
 title="Aggregate liability cap reduced from $25,000,000 to $20,000,000",
 ref="TS §11 / EL §9.2",
 ts="$25,000,000 aggregate cap per party.",
 el="$20,000,000 aggregate cap per party.",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=["With indemnity carved out (D-35), a lower cap mainly limits what Stellarion can recover from Helix (for misuse outside the field, non-compete breach, unauthorized sublicensing, non-payment) while Stellarion’s own largest exposure (indemnity) is uncapped; the combination is doubly adverse. As drafted, Helix’s unpaid fees and royalties could also count toward the cap."],
 position="Restore $25,000,000 and provide that Helix’s payment obligations (upfront fee, royalties, minimum royalty) are neither limited by nor counted toward the cap."),

dict(id="D-37", area="G. Indemnification and Limitation of Liability",
 title="Indemnity scope broadened (“infringes, misappropriates, or otherwise violates”; “arising out of or relating to”; successors and assigns) without customary IP indemnity exclusions or remedies",
 ref="TS §10 / EL §9.1",
 ts="Indemnity for third-party claims “arising from alleged infringement of intellectual property rights by the indemnifying party’s Background IP”; procedures to be set out in the Definitive Agreement; subject to the cap.",
 el="Indemnity for Losses “arising out of or relating to any claim that the Indemnifying Party’s Background IP, as contributed to or utilized in the arrangement … infringes, misappropriates, or otherwise violates” third-party IP; Indemnified Parties include successors and assigns. No exclusions; no mitigation remedies.",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=["Adding misappropriation and “otherwise violates” broadens Stellarion’s exposure beyond infringement, and “as … utilized in the arrangement” extends cover to EdgeAI as integrated, modified and combined by Helix. The letter omits standard licensor protections: no indemnity for claims caused by (a) Helix modifications (Helix has a modification right under EL §4.1), (b) combination with Helix Edge Runtime or other non-Stellarion technology, (c) use outside the Licensed Field or in breach, or (d) continued use after Stellarion supplies a non-infringing update; and no right for Stellarion to procure a license, modify or replace, or terminate and refund as its remedy. Coverage of “successors and assigns” matters given the free M&A assignment right (D-54)."],
 position="Limit to infringement or misappropriation by EdgeAI as delivered by Stellarion and used in accordance with the Agreement; add customary exclusions and procure/modify/replace/terminate remedies; keep within the cap (D-35)."),

dict(id="D-38", area="G. Indemnification and Limitation of Liability",
 title="Indemnification procedures added (prompt notice with prejudice standard; control of defense; settlement consent)",
 ref="TS §10 / EL §9.1",
 ts="Standard procedures to be set out in the Definitive Agreement.",
 el="Prompt notice (failure excuses only to the extent of material prejudice); indemnitor controls defense with counsel reasonably acceptable to the indemnitee; indemnitee “shall cooperate fully”; no settlement imposing obligations or lacking a full release without consent.",
 sev="Minor", favors="Neutral", action="Accept",
 analysis=["Market-standard and mutual. Minor refinements: cooperation at the indemnitor’s expense; a clearer standard for approval of defense counsel."],
 position="Accept with minor refinements."),

dict(id="D-39", area="G. Indemnification and Limitation of Liability",
 title="Consequential damages waiver expressly covers lost profits and revenue, with no carve-out for license scope, field-of-use, non-compete, sublicensing or payment breaches",
 ref="TS §11 / EL §9.2 (second paragraph)",
 ts="Mutual waiver of indirect, incidental, consequential, special or punitive damages. Cap exclusions: confidentiality; willful misconduct or fraud.",
 el="Waiver adds “exemplary” damages and expressly “loss of profits, loss of revenue, loss of data, loss of business opportunity, or loss of goodwill”; excepted only for the cap carve-outs (indemnity, confidentiality, willful misconduct or fraud).",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=["Stellarion’s principal damages if Helix deploys EdgeAI in supply chain optimization, breaches the non-compete or sublicenses without consent would be lost profits in its core market. Expressly waiving lost profits and lost business opportunity would bar most of that recovery, leaving injunctive relief, which the exclusive arbitration clause itself makes uncertain (D-53). The Term Sheet waiver had the same basic architecture, so part of this is a gap common to both documents, but the express listing of lost profits makes the Engagement Letter materially worse."],
 position="Carve out from both the cap and the waiver: (i) use of EdgeAI or Joint IP outside the scope of the license (including the Excluded Field); (ii) breach of the non-compete and sublicensing restrictions; (iii) infringement or misappropriation of the other party’s IP; (iv) payment obligations."),

dict(id="D-40", area="H. Confidentiality",
 title="Confidentiality survival cut from 3 years to 2 years",
 ref="TS §14 (Binding) / EL §10.2",
 ts="Survives three years after expiration or termination of the Definitive Agreement.",
 el="Survives two years after expiration or termination of “this Agreement.”",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=["Helix will receive EdgeAI technical information and co-develop alongside Stellarion engineers. A two-year tail is short for trade secrets in transformer-based ML architectures, and a contractual confidentiality obligation that expires can undercut the “reasonable measures” element of trade secret protection. The clock also runs from termination of the Engagement Letter itself, which could end soon (on supersession or 60 days’ notice)."],
 position="Restore three years minimum; trade secrets and source code protected for as long as they remain trade secrets; clarify that supersession by the Definitive Agreement does not start or end the tail."),

dict(id="D-41", area="H. Confidentiality",
 title="“Confidential Information” narrowed (designated or reasonably understood as confidential); exceptions loosened; permitted recipients expanded to consultants and contractors",
 ref="TS §14 / EL §3 (“Confidential Information”), §10.1",
 ts="All non-public technical, business, financial and other information disclosed in connection with the transactions, in any form. Prior-knowledge exception requires evidence by written records; public-domain exception requires no breach by the recipient. Disclosure to employees, directors, advisors and professional representatives with a need to know.",
 el="Information “designated as confidential or that … reasonably should be understood to be confidential”; prior-knowledge exception without written records; public-domain exception “through no fault”; disclosure also to “officers, … consultants, and contractors” bound by written obligations; compelled disclosure exception added; agreement terms expressly confidential.",
 sev="Moderate", favors="Mixed (net Helix)", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=["The marking/reasonable-understanding test is common but narrower than “all non-public information” and shifts the burden to Stellarion in a dispute. Dropping the written-records requirement makes the prior-knowledge exception easier for Helix to invoke against EdgeAI information. Permitting disclosure to consultants and contractors lets EdgeAI information reach third parties (possibly ones who also work for Stellarion competitors). The compelled disclosure exception, confidentiality of agreement terms and written-obligation requirement for recipients are acceptable or favorable."],
 position="Restore the Term Sheet definition (or deem EdgeAI technical information, source code and Stellarion roadmaps confidential regardless of marking); restore the written-records requirement; disclosure of EdgeAI technical information to contractors only with Stellarion’s prior consent; each party liable for its recipients."),

dict(id="D-42", area="H. Confidentiality",
 title="New use restriction, standard of care and return/destruction obligations (one archival copy permitted)",
 ref="TS §14 / EL §10.1",
 ts="Non-disclosure only; no express use restriction.",
 el="No use except to perform obligations or exercise rights; at least the care used for own information (no less than reasonable); return or destroy at the discloser’s election with certification; one archival copy for legal and compliance purposes.",
 sev="Minor", favors="Stellarion", action="Accept",
 analysis=["Favorable to Stellarion as the main discloser. The archival-copy exception should exclude source code and EdgeAI technical materials."],

dict(id="D-43", area="I. Termination",

  "Adding “services” extends the license from distributed product to hosted, managed and professional-services offerings (e.g., Helix-operated analytics delivered to customers), which are harder to monitor, harder to audit for royalties and easier to direct at supply chain customers. The open-ended “successive versions” definition invites Helix to argue that a re-platformed or rebranded product family, potentially including analytics products far from the edge runtime, is still “Helix Edge Runtime.”",
  "This compounds the field-of-use expansion: the broader the product perimeter, the more weight the field restriction must bear.",
 ],
 position="Revert to “Helix Edge Runtime products and related documentation.” If Helix needs a services right, limit it to hosted delivery of Helix Edge Runtime itself, within the Licensed Field, with royalties on all associated revenue. Define Helix Edge Runtime by a product description schedule; successor versions qualify only if they remain an edge compute platform of substantially the same function; merging Helix Edge Runtime into other Helix products does not expand the license."),

dict(id="D-6", area="B. License Grant, Field of Use and Term",
 title="Sublicensing of the licensed technology: consent mechanism replaced with “except as expressly set forth in this Agreement”; Affiliate use unaddressed",
 ref="TS §2 (Sublicensing) / EL §4.1, §3 (“Gross Revenue”)",
 ts="“Helix may not sublicense the licensed technology to any third party without the prior written consent of Stellarion.”",
 el="“Helix shall have no right to sublicense the rights granted hereunder except as expressly set forth in this Agreement.”",
 sev="Moderate", favors="Neutral / ambiguous", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=[
  "On its face the Engagement Letter is not less restrictive: nothing in it expressly permits sublicensing, and the escrow license in EL §12 expressly prohibits it. However, (i) “except as expressly set forth” is a hook Helix will try to fill in the Definitive Agreement (Affiliates, OEMs, channel partners, contractors); (ii) the royalty base counts revenue of Helix’s “Affiliates” (EL §3), implying Affiliate exploitation, although the license runs only to Helix; and (iii) the free M&A assignment right (EL §16.2; D-54) operates as a de facto transfer of the license without consent.",
  "Neither document addresses end-customer terms. The Definitive Agreement should require Helix to distribute EdgeAI only in object code, embedded in Helix Edge Runtime, under end-user terms at least as protective as a Stellarion-approved minimum (no reverse engineering, field restriction, no further sublicensing).",
 ],
 position="Restore the Term Sheet formulation (“Helix may not sublicense … without the prior written consent of Stellarion”); Affiliates may exercise rights only with Stellarion’s consent, with Helix liable for their compliance; add minimum end-user license terms."),

dict(id="D-9", area="B. License Grant, Field of Use and Term",
 title="Renewal: two 3-year renewal terms (maximum 11 years) instead of two 2-year terms (maximum 9 years); non-renewal notice cut from 180 to 120 days",

 ],

dict(id="D-10", area="C. Financial Terms",
 title="Upfront fee installments restructured from $7.5M / $5.0M to two equal $6.25M installments",
 ref="TS §4.1 / EL §5.1",
 ts="$12,500,000 total: $7,500,000 due upon execution of the Definitive Agreement; $5,000,000 due on the six-month anniversary.",
 el="$12,500,000 total: $6,250,000 within 10 business days following execution of the Definitive Agreement; $6,250,000 on the six-month anniversary.",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=[
  "The headline number is unchanged, which makes this easy to miss on a skim. But $1,250,000 moves from the signing installment to the six-month installment, increasing Stellarion’s credit exposure to Helix on the deferred tranche from $5.0 million to $6.25 million (25% more) and deferring cash Stellarion expected at closing. Illustratively, at an 8% annual cost of capital the time-value cost of the shift alone is about $48,000, before credit risk and the extra 10-business-day delay on the first installment (D-11).",
  "Stellarion’s protection on the deferred tranche is also weak: no acceleration on Helix termination, assignment or change of control, and no late-payment interest outside the audit context (D-19).",
 ],
 position="Restore $7,500,000 on execution and $5,000,000 at six months. Add acceleration of the second installment on any termination by Helix (other than for Stellarion’s uncured breach), any termination by Stellarion for Helix breach or insolvency, and any assignment by Helix under the M&A exception."),

dict(id="D-12", area="C. Financial Terms",
 title="Royalty base changed from Net Revenue (received, less returns, allowances, trade discounts, sales taxes) to Gross Revenue (GAAP-recognized revenue of Helix and its Affiliates, before any deductions)",
 ref="TS §4.2 / EL §3 (“Gross Revenue”), §5.2",
 ts="4.5% of Net Revenue: “gross revenue actually received by Helix … less returns, allowances, trade discounts, and sales taxes actually incurred.”",
 el="4.5% of Gross Revenue: “all revenue recognized by Helix or its Affiliates” from products and services that “incorporate or utilize” EdgeAI, under GAAP, “prior to any deductions for returns, allowances, discounts, shipping, taxes, or other adjustments.”",
 sev="Minor", favors="Stellarion", action="Accept",
 analysis=[
  "This deviation favors Stellarion: the rate is unchanged but the base is larger (no deductions), includes Affiliate revenue, covers products that merely “utilize” EdgeAI, and is measured on recognition rather than cash receipt. Illustratively, on $50 million of attributable gross revenue with 8% deductions, the Engagement Letter royalty is $2.25 million against $2.07 million under the Term Sheet (about $180,000 more per year).",
  "Cautions: (i) Helix may have intended this as a trade for other concessions (e.g., the lower minimum royalty), or it may be an error Helix will reverse once noticed; (ii) GAAP recognition for subscription offerings is ratable, which can defer royalties relative to billings; (iii) “attributable to” is undefined, so for bundled offerings Helix will argue only a fraction of the bundle price is attributable. The Definitive Agreement needs an allocation method (e.g., royalty on the full price of any SKU that includes EdgeAI functionality, or a per-unit minimum).",
  "Negotiating posture: Stellarion’s overall message is “conform to the Term Sheet,” and holding on to a Stellarion-favorable deviation slightly weakens that message. We recommend retaining Gross Revenue in the redline as a tradable item that can be conceded (reverting to Net Revenue) in exchange for restoration of the dealbreaker items.",
 ],
 position="Accept (retain) in the redline; add a bundled-revenue allocation rule and extend audit rights to Affiliates. Be prepared to revert to Term Sheet Net Revenue as a concession."),

dict(id="D-25", area="D. Project Meridian Co-Development",
 title="“Joint IP” narrowed to IP jointly created by both parties’ personnel; Meridian IP created by one party alone falls outside joint ownership",
 ref="TS §5.3 (“Co-Developed IP”) / EL §3 (“Joint IP”), §6.3",
 ts="“All intellectual property arising from Project Meridian, including all inventions, discoveries, improvements, works of authorship, software, algorithms, and related documentation” is jointly owned.",
 el="Joint IP is IP “conceived, created, developed, or reduced to practice jointly by employees or contractors of both Parties in the course of, and arising from, Project Meridian.” No rule for IP created by one party alone.",
 sev="Material", favors="Ambiguous (likely Helix)", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=[
  "Under the Term Sheet everything arising from Project Meridian is joint; under the Engagement Letter only jointly-created IP is joint, and Meridian work product created by one party’s team alone would by default belong to the creating party. Helix is likely to perform most of the integration engineering on Helix Edge Runtime, so this gap could leave Helix as sole owner of significant Meridian deliverables, free of any sublicensing restriction at all.",
  "The narrower definition also interacts with the Background IP boundary (D-27): EdgeAI improvements Stellarion makes alone during Meridian fall outside Joint IP (good for Stellarion) but may also fall outside Stellarion Background IP if any Helix “resources” were used.",
  "A related gap exists in both documents: neither carves out improvements to, or derivatives of, a party’s Background IP from co-developed IP. Under the Term Sheet’s broad definition, improvements to EdgeAI arising from Meridian would be jointly owned. The Definitive Agreement should provide that improvements and derivatives of Stellarion Background IP (including EdgeAI) vest solely in Stellarion, and of Helix Background IP solely in Helix, with the rest of the Meridian output jointly owned.",
 ],
 position="Restore the Term Sheet scope (all IP arising from Project Meridian), subject to a carve-out that improvements, modifications and derivatives of a party’s Background IP belong to that party, with a license back for Meridian purposes only."),

dict(id="D-26", area="D. Project Meridian Co-Development",

dict(id="D-27", area="E. Background IP",
 title="“Background IP” redefined: includes IP “licensed to” a party; measured at the Engagement Letter date; independently developed IP excluded if it uses any of the other party’s Confidential Information or “resources”",
 ref="TS §6 / EL §3 (“Background IP”), §7",
 ts="All pre-existing IP of each party, and IP developed by it “prior to or independently of the co-development activities,” remains that party’s sole property.",
 el="Background IP is IP “owned by or licensed to a Party as of the Effective Date, or developed or acquired by a Party independently of this Agreement and without use of the other Party’s Confidential Information or resources.” Ownership language in §7 otherwise tracks the Term Sheet and adds “by implication, estoppel, or otherwise.”",
 sev="Moderate", favors="Mixed", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=["(i) “Licensed to”: Background IP is the trigger for each party’s indemnity (EL §9.1), so including in-licensed IP expands Stellarion’s indemnity to third-party components in EdgeAI (open source or commercial libraries), uncapped under EL §9.2 (D-35). (iii) The added “by implication, estoppel, or otherwise” language helps Stellarion and should be kept."],
 position="Define Stellarion Background IP to include EdgeAI and all improvements, modifications and derivatives of it however and whenever developed; delete “or resources”; decouple the indemnity trigger from in-licensed IP (D-37)."),

 el="Survival list covers §§3, 5 (accrued payments), 7, 9, 9.2, 10, 15 and 16. Section 8 is not listed.",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=["Although EL §8.1 refers to a post-termination period, an express survival clause listing specific sections invites the argument (expressio unius) that unlisted provisions, including §8.1, do not survive. A post-term restriction whose survival is disputed is worth much less. Whether oversight or deliberate, it must be fixed."],
 position="Add “Section 8.1 (Helix Non-Compete), for the Non-Compete Period” to the survival list (see also D-46)."),

dict(id="D-32", area="F. Non-Compete, Exclusivity and MFN",
 title="Stellarion exclusivity period shortened from 24 to 18 months",
 ref="TS §8 (Binding) / EL §8.2",
 ts="24 months from the Effective Date; a Binding Provision.",
 el="18 months from the Effective Date (now the Engagement Letter date).",
 sev="Minor", favors="Stellarion", action="Accept",
 analysis=["This shortens a restriction on Stellarion and is Stellarion-favorable. Notes: (i) because the Effective Date moves earlier (D-2), the 18 months also start sooner; (ii) the Term Sheet exclusivity is a Binding Provision that the Engagement Letter would supersede; (iii) if the MFN is reinstated with its Term Sheet link to “the exclusivity period” (D-34), the MFN window would also be 18 months. Helix may notice and ask to revert to 24 months; as that is the Term Sheet position, Stellarion should not resist it strongly."],
 position="Accept 18 months; do not spend leverage defending it."),

dict(id="D-33", area="F. Non-Compete, Exclusivity and MFN",
 title="Restricted Competitor Schedule (Schedule A) deferred to the Definitive Agreement; interim good faith identification; safe harbor shifts from “not listed” to “not a direct competitor”",
 ref="TS §8 / EL §8.2",
 ts="Schedule to be negotiated in good faith and “finalized prior to execution of the Definitive Agreement”; Stellarion free to license to “any party not listed” on the schedule.",
 el="Schedule A “shall be negotiated and finalized … as part of the Definitive Agreement”; pending finalization the parties cooperate in good faith to identify direct competitors; Stellarion free to license to “any Person that is not a direct competitor of Helix.” Schedule A is referred to as attached “hereto” but is not attached.",
 sev="Moderate", favors="Helix", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=["In the interim there is no list, so the restriction is either empty (no one is “listed on Schedule A”) or, as Helix will argue from the final sentence, applies to any “direct competitor of Helix,” an undefined and potentially broad category given Helix’s breadth (data lakes, streaming pipelines, edge compute). The Term Sheet’s “not listed” safe harbor was a bright line; the Engagement Letter clouds Stellarion’s freedom to license EdgeAI in the interim."],
 position="Attach an agreed Schedule A now (preferred), or state that until it is attached no Person is restricted; restore “not listed on Schedule A” as the safe harbor; cap the list (e.g., no more than eight to ten named entities, excluding their non-competing affiliates)."),

dict(id="D-34", area="F. Non-Compete, Exclusivity and MFN",
 title="MOST-FAVORED-NATION provision omitted entirely [GC PRIORITY 3]",
 ref="TS §9 / EL — (no corresponding provision)",
 ts="During the exclusivity period, if Stellarion licenses EdgeAI to a third party (other than Restricted Competitors) on terms more favorable “taken as a whole,” Stellarion must notify Helix and offer those terms; 30 days to elect; 30 days to implement.",
 el="No MFN provision. The supersession language (EL §1) and integration clause (EL §16.3) would extinguish TS §9.",
 sev="Material", favors="Stellarion on its face; creates risk", action="Flag for further discussion",
 analysis=["See Part IV.3 for the full analysis."],
 position="Flag for discussion. Our recommendation is to reinstate the Term Sheet MFN in its narrow form, expressly tied as consideration to a restored 18-month non-compete (Part IV.3; Appendix A-3)."),

dict(id="D-35", area="G. Indemnification and Limitation of Liability",
 title="Indemnification carved OUT of the liability cap (uncapped), reversing the Term Sheet’s express statement that indemnity is within the cap",
 ref="TS §10, §11 / EL §9.2",
 ts="“For the avoidance of doubt, indemnification obligations under Section 10 are subject to and included within the aggregate liability cap.” Only exclusions: confidentiality breaches; willful misconduct or fraud.",
 el="Cap does not apply to “(A) a Party’s indemnification obligations under Section 9.1,” confidentiality breaches, or willful misconduct or fraud. The consequential damages waiver also does not apply to these carve-outs.",
 sev="Dealbreaker", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=[
  "The indemnity is mutual in form but asymmetric in substance. Stellarion contributes the core licensed technology, which Helix will distribute worldwide across roughly 3,400 enterprise customers, so Stellarion’s IP indemnity is the obligation most likely to be called. Removing it from the cap and from the consequential damages waiver exposes Stellarion to unlimited liability, including customers’ consequential losses passed through as third-party claims, in exchange for a $12.5 million upfront fee. For a company with $67.3 million ARR, a single significant patent assertion against Helix’s installed base could exceed Stellarion’s total consideration under the deal.",
  "The Term Sheet language was explicit (“for the avoidance of doubt … included within”), so this is a direct reversal of a negotiated point, not a gap-fill.",
 ],
 position="Reject. Restore: indemnification obligations are subject to and included within the aggregate cap. If Helix insists on separate treatment, at most consider a separate IP indemnity super-cap no higher than the $25 million general cap, with customary exclusions and remedies (D-37)."),

dict(id="D-36", area="G. Indemnification and Limitation of Liability",
 title="Aggregate liability cap reduced from $25,000,000 to $20,000,000",
 ref="TS §11 / EL §9.2",
 ts="$25,000,000 aggregate cap per party.",
 el="$20,000,000 aggregate cap per party.",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=["With indemnity carved out (D-35), a lower cap mainly limits what Stellarion can recover from Helix (for misuse outside the field, non-compete breach, unauthorized sublicensing, non-payment) while Stellarion’s own largest exposure (indemnity) is uncapped; the combination is doubly adverse. As drafted, Helix’s unpaid fees and royalties could also count toward the cap."],
 position="Restore $25,000,000 and provide that Helix’s payment obligations (upfront fee, royalties, minimum royalty) are neither limited by nor counted toward the cap."),

dict(id="D-37", area="G. Indemnification and Limitation of Liability",
 title="Indemnity scope broadened (“infringes, misappropriates, or otherwise violates”; “arising out of or relating to”; successors and assigns) without customary IP indemnity exclusions or remedies",
 ref="TS §10 / EL §9.1",
 ts="Indemnity for third-party claims “arising from alleged infringement of intellectual property rights by the indemnifying party’s Background IP”; procedures to be set out in the Definitive Agreement; subject to the cap.",
 el="Indemnity for Losses “arising out of or relating to any claim that the Indemnifying Party’s Background IP, as contributed to or utilized in the arrangement … infringes, misappropriates, or otherwise violates” third-party IP; Indemnified Parties include successors and assigns. No exclusions; no mitigation remedies.",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=["Adding misappropriation and “otherwise violates” broadens Stellarion’s exposure beyond infringement, and “as … utilized in the arrangement” extends cover to EdgeAI as integrated, modified and combined by Helix. The letter omits standard licensor protections: no indemnity for claims caused by (a) Helix modifications (Helix has a modification right under EL §4.1), (b) combination with Helix Edge Runtime or other non-Stellarion technology, (c) use outside the Licensed Field or in breach, or (d) continued use after Stellarion supplies a non-infringing update; and no right for Stellarion to procure a license, modify or replace, or terminate and refund as its remedy. Coverage of “successors and assigns” matters given the free M&A assignment right (D-54)."],
 position="Limit to infringement or misappropriation by EdgeAI as delivered by Stellarion and used in accordance with the Agreement; add customary exclusions and procure/modify/replace/terminate remedies; keep within the cap (D-35)."),

dict(id="D-38", area="G. Indemnification and Limitation of Liability",
 title="Indemnification procedures added (prompt notice with prejudice standard; control of defense; settlement consent)",
 ref="TS §10 / EL §9.1",
 ts="Standard procedures to be set out in the Definitive Agreement.",
 el="Prompt notice (failure excuses only to the extent of material prejudice); indemnitor controls defense with counsel reasonably acceptable to the indemnitee; indemnitee “shall cooperate fully”; no settlement imposing obligations or lacking a full release without consent.",
 sev="Minor", favors="Neutral", action="Accept",
 analysis=["Market-standard and mutual. Minor refinements: cooperation at the indemnitor’s expense; a clearer standard for approval of defense counsel."],
 position="Accept with minor refinements."),

dict(id="D-39", area="G. Indemnification and Limitation of Liability",
 title="Consequential damages waiver expressly covers lost profits and revenue, with no carve-out for license scope, field-of-use, non-compete, sublicensing or payment breaches",
 ref="TS §11 / EL §9.2 (second paragraph)",
 ts="Mutual waiver of indirect, incidental, consequential, special or punitive damages. Cap exclusions: confidentiality; willful misconduct or fraud.",
 el="Waiver adds “exemplary” damages and expressly “loss of profits, loss of revenue, loss of data, loss of business opportunity, or loss of goodwill”; excepted only for the cap carve-outs (indemnity, confidentiality, willful misconduct or fraud).",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=["Stellarion’s principal damages if Helix deploys EdgeAI in supply chain optimization, breaches the non-compete or sublicenses without consent would be lost profits in its core market. Expressly waiving lost profits and lost business opportunity would bar most of that recovery, leaving injunctive relief, which the exclusive arbitration clause itself makes uncertain (D-53). The Term Sheet waiver had the same basic architecture, so part of this is a gap common to both documents, but the express listing of lost profits makes the Engagement Letter materially worse."],
 position="Carve out from both the cap and the waiver: (i) use of EdgeAI or Joint IP outside the scope of the license (including the Excluded Field); (ii) breach of the non-compete and sublicensing restrictions; (iii) infringement or misappropriation of the other party’s IP; (iv) payment obligations."),

dict(id="D-40", area="H. Confidentiality",
 title="Confidentiality survival cut from 3 years to 2 years",
 ref="TS §14 (Binding) / EL §10.2",
 ts="Survives three years after expiration or termination of the Definitive Agreement.",
 el="Survives two years after expiration or termination of “this Agreement.”",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=["Helix will receive EdgeAI technical information and co-develop alongside Stellarion engineers. A two-year tail is short for trade secrets in transformer-based ML architectures, and a contractual confidentiality obligation that expires can undercut the “reasonable measures” element of trade secret protection. The clock also runs from termination of the Engagement Letter itself, which could end soon (on supersession or 60 days’ notice)."],
 position="Restore three years minimum; trade secrets and source code protected for as long as they remain trade secrets; clarify that supersession by the Definitive Agreement does not start or end the tail."),

dict(id="D-41", area="H. Confidentiality",
 title="“Confidential Information” narrowed (designated or reasonably understood as confidential); exceptions loosened; permitted recipients expanded to consultants and contractors",
 ref="TS §14 / EL §3 (“Confidential Information”), §10.1",
 ts="All non-public technical, business, financial and other information disclosed in connection with the transactions, in any form. Prior-knowledge exception requires evidence by written records; public-domain exception requires no breach by the recipient. Disclosure to employees, directors, advisors and professional representatives with a need to know.",
 el="Information “designated as confidential or that … reasonably should be understood to be confidential”; prior-knowledge exception without written records; public-domain exception “through no fault”; disclosure also to “officers, … consultants, and contractors” bound by written obligations; compelled disclosure exception added; agreement terms expressly confidential.",
 sev="Moderate", favors="Mixed (net Helix)", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=["The marking/reasonable-understanding test is common but narrower than “all non-public information” and shifts the burden to Stellarion in a dispute. Dropping the written-records requirement makes the prior-knowledge exception easier for Helix to invoke against EdgeAI information. Permitting disclosure to consultants and contractors lets EdgeAI information reach third parties (possibly ones who also work for Stellarion competitors). The compelled disclosure exception, confidentiality of agreement terms and written-obligation requirement for recipients are acceptable or favorable."],
 position="Restore the Term Sheet definition (or deem EdgeAI technical information, source code and Stellarion roadmaps confidential regardless of marking); restore the written-records requirement; disclosure of EdgeAI technical information to contractors only with Stellarion’s prior consent; each party liable for its recipients."),

dict(id="D-42", area="H. Confidentiality",
 title="New use restriction, standard of care and return/destruction obligations (one archival copy permitted)",
 ref="TS §14 / EL §10.1",
 ts="Non-disclosure only; no express use restriction.",
 el="No use except to perform obligations or exercise rights; at least the care used for own information (no less than reasonable); return or destroy at the discloser’s election with certification; one archival copy for legal and compliance purposes.",
 sev="Minor", favors="Stellarion", action="Accept",
 analysis=["Favorable to Stellarion as the main discloser. The archival-copy exception should exclude source code and EdgeAI technical materials."],
 position="Accept, excluding source code and EdgeAI technical documentation from the archival copy right."),

dict(id="D-43", area="I. Termination",
 title="Breach termination: 30-day notice running concurrently with a 30-day cure (about 30 days) instead of 60-day notice plus 30-day cure (90 days); double materiality qualifier",
 ref="TS §12.1 / EL §11.1",
 ts="60 days’ written notice; 30-day cure period; termination effective at the end of the cure period, “i.e., ninety (90) days total from delivery of the initial notice of breach.”",
 el="Termination on 30 days’ prior written notice for “a material breach … of any material provision,” if uncured 30 days after receipt of notice.",
 sev="Moderate", favors="Mixed", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=[
  "The timeline compresses from about 90 days to about 30. Because the right is mutual, it cuts both ways: Stellarion could terminate faster for Helix breaches (non-payment, field-of-use violations), but Helix could also terminate quickly (for example over a Meridian dispute) shortly after Stellarion has deposited source code and committed development resources. The double qualifier (“material breach” of a “material provision”) raises the bar to terminate and is generally unhelpful to a licensor.",
  "Term Sheet drafting note: TS §12.1 is internally inconsistent. A 30-day cure running “following receipt of such notice” expires on day 30, not day 90; the parenthetical shows the intended reading (60-day notice period followed by a 30-day cure). The Definitive Agreement should state the mechanics unambiguously.",
 ],
 position="Split regime: (i) payment defaults: 15 to 30 day cure, then termination; (ii) breaches of the field-of-use, sublicensing, confidentiality or non-compete provisions: 30 days if curable, immediate if not curable or willful; (iii) other material breaches: the Term Sheet 90-day framework. Delete “of any material provision.”"),

dict(id="D-44", area="I. Termination",
 title="Insolvency termination: 60-day dismissal window for involuntary petitions; “general” assignment; “all or a substantial portion” of assets",
 ref="TS §12.2 / EL §11.2",
 ts="Immediate termination on insolvency, bankruptcy petition (voluntary or involuntary), assignment for the benefit of creditors, or receiver for substantially all assets.",
 el="Same triggers, but involuntary petitions count only if not dismissed within 60 days; receiver trigger extends to “all or a substantial portion” of assets.",
 sev="Minor", favors="Neutral", action="Accept",
 analysis=["Market-standard and mutual. Ipso facto termination rights may be unenforceable against a debtor under the U.S. Bankruptcy Code, and Helix as licensee would have rights under 11 U.S.C. §365(n) if Stellarion were the debtor; neither point is a reason to reject the clause."],
 position="Accept."),

dict(id="D-45", area="I. Termination",
 title="New 90-day Wind-Down Period on any expiration or termination (including for Helix breach); royalties on wind-down sales not addressed",
 ref="TS §12.3(a), (b) / EL §11.3",
 ts="License ends “subject to any wind-down period to be agreed upon in the Definitive Agreement”; Helix “shall immediately cease” all use, reproduction and distribution.",
 el="Helix must cease use within 90 days and may continue distribution during that period to fulfil orders accepted before termination; applies to termination “for any reason.”",
 sev="Moderate", favors="Helix", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=["A 90-day wind-down is not unusual, but (i) it applies even where Stellarion terminates for Helix’s breach, including field-of-use or sublicensing violations; (ii) Running Royalties are payable “during the License Term” (EL §5.2), so Helix may argue no royalty is owed on wind-down sales; and (iii) existing customer deployments are not addressed."],
 position="Wind-down only for expiration or termination other than for Helix’s breach; royalties expressly payable on all wind-down revenue; no new customers; all license restrictions, including the Excluded Field, continue to apply."),

dict(id="D-46", area="I. Termination",
 title="Survival list omits Joint IP (§6.3), reservation of rights (§4.3), wind-down terms and escrow post-release limits (§12); lists §9 and §9.2 redundantly",
 ref="TS §12.3 / EL §11.3",
 ts="Accrued payments, non-compete and confidentiality survive.",
 el="Survival of §§3, 5 (accrued payments only), 7, 9, 9.2, 10 (subject to §10.2), 15, 16.",
 sev="Moderate", favors="Ambiguous", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=["Beyond the non-compete (D-31), the list omits the Joint IP provisions (which must survive for ownership and, once restored, for the sublicensing consent requirement), the reservation of rights, the limits on released escrow materials, and royalties on wind-down sales. Because the Definitive Agreement “shall supersede this Engagement Letter in its entirety” (EL §14), the parties should also confirm that accrued rights and obligations carry over."],
 position="Add §4.3, §6.3, §8.1, §11.3 (wind-down), §12 (post-release limits) and royalties on wind-down sales to the survival list."),

dict(id="D-47", area="J. Source Code Escrow",
 title="Source code deposit due within 30 days of the Engagement Letter Effective Date (before the Definitive Agreement and before any payment)",
 ref="TS §13 / EL §12",
 ts="Three-party escrow agreement “to be executed contemporaneously with the Definitive Agreement.”",
 el="Deposit within 30 days following the Effective Date (the Engagement Letter date) under a three-party agreement “to be entered into”; costs shared equally.",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=["Stellarion would have to place its crown-jewel source code, build scripts, tools and documentation in escrow for Helix’s benefit before a Definitive Agreement exists, before Helix pays anything, and possibly before the escrow agreement terms are settled. If the Definitive Agreement fails, Stellarion would have to unwind the deposit."],
 position="Deposit within 30 days after the later of execution of the Definitive Agreement and the three-party escrow agreement and receipt of the first upfront installment."),

dict(id="D-48", area="J. Source Code Escrow",
 title="Release conditions changed: insolvency trigger narrowed to bankruptcy filings; uncured material breach trigger deleted; discontinuation trigger redefined (no 12-month cessation period, but a successor-product cure added)",
 ref="TS §13(a)–(c) / EL §12",
 ts="Release only on (a) bankruptcy or insolvency as described in TS §12.2; (b) Stellarion material breach uncured after notice and cure; (c) discontinuation, meaning Stellarion ceases to actively develop, maintain and support EdgeAI for a continuous period of 12 months or more.",
 el="Release only on (a) a Stellarion bankruptcy filing, or an involuntary petition not dismissed within 60 days; or (b) Stellarion “discontinues the Stellarion EdgeAI™ product line and fails to provide a commercially reasonable successor product within one hundred twenty (120) days.”",
 sev="Moderate", favors="Mixed (net Stellarion)", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=["Deleting the breach trigger and narrowing the insolvency trigger favor Stellarion and should be accepted. The discontinuation trigger is mixed: the successor-product cure helps Stellarion, but the objective 12-month cessation test is replaced by an undefined “discontinues the … product line,” which Helix could try to apply to end-of-life of a version or a rebranding, with release possible after only 120 days."],
 position="Accept (a) and the deletion of the breach trigger; for discontinuation, combine both protections: release only if Stellarion ceases to actively develop, maintain and support EdgeAI for a continuous 12 months and does not make available a commercially reasonable successor product."),

dict(id="D-49", area="J. Source Code Escrow",
 title="Escrow scope and mechanics: build materials included; updates only with each major release; written verification; costs shared equally; post-release license for internal maintenance only",
 ref="TS §13 / EL §12",
 ts="Deposit source code “and all updates thereto”; deposit frequency, verification and release procedures to be in the escrow agreement.",
 el="Escrowed Materials include build scripts, libraries, tools and documentation; updates with each major release; written verification; costs borne equally; after release, a non-exclusive, non-transferable license for internal maintenance and support only, with no distribution or sublicensing of source code.",
 sev="Minor", favors="Mixed (net Stellarion)", action="Accept",
 analysis=["Major-release-only updates reduce Stellarion’s burden compared with “all updates,” and the post-release limits are favorable. Equal cost sharing is a new allocation (the beneficiary customarily pays). The post-release license should confirm that field-of-use, confidentiality and royalty obligations continue."],
 position="Accept; propose that Helix bear escrow fees; released materials remain Stellarion Confidential Information subject to the Licensed Field and continuing royalties."),

dict(id="D-50", area="K. Representations and Warranties",
 title="New representations and warranties (including Stellarion sole ownership, knowledge-qualified non-infringement and no-claims representations) and disclaimer",
 ref="TS §16 (reps to Definitive Agreement) / EL §13",
 ts="Representations and warranties to be included in the Definitive Agreement.",
 el="Mutual organization and authority reps; Stellarion: sole owner of EdgeAI free and clear of liens, non-infringing to its knowledge, no pending or (to its knowledge) threatened claims, full right to grant; Helix: owns Helix Edge Runtime, non-infringing to its knowledge, has resources for Meridian. Broad disclaimer.",
 sev="Moderate", favors="Helix (asymmetric)", action="Flag for further discussion",
 analysis=["The Stellarion representations are not unreasonable in principle, but they are given now, in an interim letter, and are asymmetric (Helix gives no no-claims or full-right representation). Before signing, Stellarion should confirm: (i) no lender liens or security interests over its IP (a routine IP security interest under a credit facility would breach a “free and clear” representation); (ii) open source and third-party components in EdgeAI (“sole and exclusive owner of all right, title, and interest” is inaccurate if EdgeAI includes licensed components); and (iii) no existing license, exclusivity or MFN granted to anyone else conflicts with the Helix grant (mutual rep 13.1(d)). The disclaimer helps Stellarion and should be kept."],
 position="Move substantive IP representations to the Definitive Agreement; if given now, qualify them by a disclosure schedule, limit “sole owner” to Stellarion-developed components, disclose liens and open source, and make the no-claims representation mutual."),

dict(id="D-51", area="L. Definitive Agreement",
 title="Definitive Agreement to include new categories: warranty terms, service levels, support and maintenance, data security, insurance",
 ref="TS §16 / EL §14",
 ts="Additional customary provisions, “including representations and warranties, conditions to closing, and such other terms as the parties may agree.”",
 el="Additional terms “customary for transactions of this nature, including without limitation … warranty terms, service level commitments, support and maintenance obligations, data security requirements, insurance provisions.”",
 sev="Moderate", favors="Helix", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=["Listing service levels, support and maintenance as agreed categories signals that Stellarion will owe operational support commitments the Term Sheet economics did not price. Helix will cite this binding text to argue that Stellarion agreed in principle to provide them."],
 position="Replace with “such additional terms as the Parties may mutually agree,” and state that any Stellarion support, maintenance or service level obligations will be subject to separate agreement and fees."),

dict(id="D-52", area="M. Governing Law and Dispute Resolution",
 title="Arbitration mechanics: arbitrators selected under JAMS rules rather than the Term Sheet party-appointment timetable; expertise requirement; arbitrability delegated; confidentiality added; English language omitted",
 ref="TS §15 (Binding) / EL §15",
 ts="Delaware law; JAMS; seat Wilmington; three arbitrators: each party appoints one within 30 days and the two appoint the third within 15 days; English language.",
 el="Delaware law; JAMS Comprehensive Rules; seat Wilmington; three arbitrators “selected in accordance with the applicable JAMS rules”; technology licensing expertise; arbitrability for the arbitrators; confidential proceedings.",
 sev="Minor", favors="Neutral", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=["Core terms (Delaware law, JAMS, Wilmington, three arbitrators) are preserved. The party-appointment timetable gives way to JAMS default selection; the confidentiality and expertise additions are acceptable. Restoring the Term Sheet selection mechanics and English language is a simple conforming change."],
 position="Restore the Term Sheet selection mechanics and English language; accept the confidentiality, expertise and delegation language."),

dict(id="D-53", area="M. Governing Law and Dispute Resolution",
 title="No carve-out for injunctive relief in court; Steering Committee “dispute resolution” overlaps with arbitration (a gap in both documents)",
 ref="TS §15 / EL §15.2, §6.1",
 ts="All disputes to binding JAMS arbitration; no injunctive relief carve-out.",
 el="All disputes “resolved exclusively by binding arbitration”; no injunctive relief carve-out; Steering Committee charged with resolving co-development disputes.",
 sev="Moderate", favors="Helix", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=["For an IP licensor, the most important remedy for field-of-use, confidentiality, sublicensing and non-compete breaches is a fast injunction. “Exclusively” makes it harder to seek a TRO in court. The gap also exists in the Term Sheet, but it matters more now that the consequential damages waiver would bar most monetary recovery for those breaches (D-39)."],
 position="Add that either party may seek temporary, preliminary or permanent injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to protect its IP or Confidential Information or to enforce §§4.1, 6.3 and 8; acknowledge irreparable harm for such breaches; Steering Committee escalation precedes but does not replace arbitration."),

dict(id="D-54", area="N. General Provisions",
 title="Assignment: consent “not unreasonably withheld,” and free assignment without consent on a merger, consolidation, reorganization or sale of substantially all assets",
 ref="TS §18 (No Assignment) / EL §16.2",
 ts="No assignment without the prior written consent of the other party; non-consensual assignment void.",
 el="Consent not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed; either party may assign without consent in a merger, consolidation, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all assets, if the assignee agrees in writing to be bound.",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=[
  "The M&A exception lets Helix transfer the EdgeAI license, its Joint IP rights and its escrow rights to an acquirer without Stellarion’s consent, including a Stellarion competitor in supply chain analytics or an ML inference vendor. A change of control of Helix (e.g., a stock acquisition) is not addressed at all. This is a backdoor around the sublicensing and field-of-use protections and the non-compete, since an acquirer’s existing competing engine business would not clearly be bound.",
  "Balancing point: the exception is mutual, and Stellarion, as the smaller company, may value its own freedom to be acquired without Helix’s consent. The recommended fix is therefore targeted rather than a blanket reversion.",
 ],
 position="Either restore the Term Sheet (consent required) or, preferably, keep a mutual M&A exception subject to: (i) no assignment by Helix to a Stellarion competitor (defined list or category, including supply chain analytics and ML inference providers) without consent; (ii) a Stellarion right to terminate, with acceleration of unpaid fees, on a Helix change of control in favor of such a competitor; (iii) the license and field limit do not extend to the acquirer’s other businesses, and the non-compete binds the acquirer’s group with respect to the Helix business."),

dict(id="D-55", area="N. General Provisions",
 title="Notices: detailed delivery mechanics; copy to Helix’s counsel but none to Stellarion’s counsel",
 ref="TS §18 (Notices), §3.2 / EL §16.1",
 ts="Written notice to the Section 1.1 addresses.",
 el="Personal delivery, overnight courier or certified mail; Stellarion attention General Counsel; Helix attention General Counsel with a copy to Hargrove, Tilden & Strauss LLP (Rachel Moynihan). No email notice.",
 sev="Minor", favors="Helix", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=["Conforming change: add a copy to Clearfield Locke LLP (Thomas Whitaker; Emily Chen-Ramirez), 555 Mission Street, 34th Floor, San Francisco, CA 94105. Non-renewal, breach and termination notices are time-critical; consider email with confirmation."],
 position="Add a Clearfield Locke copy; consider email notice with confirmation."),

dict(id="D-56", area="N. General Provisions",
 title="New force majeure clause (payment obligations excluded; includes internet and telecommunications failures; no long-stop termination right)",
 ref="TS — / EL §16.8",
 ts="Silent.",
 el="Mutual excuse for events beyond reasonable control, other than payment obligations; notice and mitigation.",
 sev="Minor", favors="Neutral", action="Accept",
 analysis=["Market-standard; the payment carve-out is appropriate. Consider excluding confidentiality, field-of-use, sublicensing and non-compete obligations (which cannot sensibly be excused) and adding a termination right if a force majeure event lasts more than 90 days."],
 position="Accept with those refinements."),

dict(id="D-57", area="N. General Provisions",
 title="New boilerplate: relationship of the parties, severability (with reformation), waiver; counterparts updated",
 ref="TS §18 / EL §§16.4–16.7",
